title.zh: 卷55 游明根 劉芳
title.raw: 卷55 游明根 劉芳 Volume 55: You Minggen, Liu Fang

sentences.zh: 游明根 劉芳

translations.literal: You Minggen, Liu Fang
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen and Liu Fang

sentences.zh: 游明根，字志遠，廣平任人也。

translations.literal: You Minggen, styled Zhiyuan, was a man of Ren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: You Minggen, whose courtesy name was Zhiyuan, was a native of Ren County in Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖鱓，慕容熙樂浪太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shan was Murong Xi's Governor of Lelang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shan served Murong Xi of Later Yan as Governor of Lelang.

sentences.zh: 父幼，馮跋假廣平太守。

translations.literal: His father You was Feng Ba's acting Governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: His father You served as acting Governor of Guangping under Feng Ba of Northern Yan.

sentences.zh: 和龍平，明根乃得歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Helong was pacified, Minggen was able to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After Helong was pacified, Minggen was at last able to return to his native place.

sentences.zh: 游雅稱薦之，世祖擢為中書學生。

translations.literal: You Ya praised and recommended him, and the Emperor Taiwu promoted him to student at the Palace Secretariat school.
translations.idiomatic: You Ya praised and recommended him, and Emperor Taiwu selected him as a student at the Palace Secretariat school.

sentences.zh: 性貞慎寡欲，綜習經典。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, cautious, and sparing of desire, and he studied the classics comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and cautious, with few desires, and he mastered the classical canon.

sentences.zh: 及恭宗監國，與公孫叡俱為主書。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Huang supervised the state, he and Gongsun Rui both served as recorders.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Huang was put in charge of state affairs, he and Gongsun Rui both served as chief recorders.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，[1]遷都曹主書，賜爵安樂男、寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne,[1] he was transferred to chief recorder in the Secretariat, and was granted the title Baron of Anle and the rank General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne,[1] Minggen was promoted to chief recorder in the Secretariat and granted the title Baron of Anle and the rank General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 高宗以其小心敬慎，每嗟美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng, because of his carefulness and reverence, often sighed in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng often sighed in admiration of his scrupulous and reverent conduct.

sentences.zh: 假員外散騎常侍、冠軍將軍、安樂侯，使於劉駿，直使明僧暠相對。

translations.literal: He was made acting Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General Who Establishes Might, and Marquis of Anle, and sent as envoy to Liu Jun, with the chief envoy Ming Senghao as his counterpart.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General Who Establishes Might, and Marquis of Anle, and sent on embassy to Liu Jun; the chief Song envoy was Ming Senghao, who served as his opposite number.

sentences.zh: 前後三返，駿稱其長者，迎送之禮，有加常使。

translations.literal: He went back and forth three times; Jun called him a man of stature, and the ceremonies of welcome and send-off exceeded those for ordinary envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He made the journey three times in all. Liu Jun called him a man of true stature, and the ceremonies of welcome and farewell went beyond those accorded ordinary envoys.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初，以本將軍出為東青州刺史，加員外常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign, with his existing rank as general he went out as Governor of Eastern Qing Province and was given the additional title of acting Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xianwen's reign he left the capital as Governor of Eastern Qing Province, retaining his general's rank and receiving the additional title of acting Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、平東將軍、都督兗州諸軍事、瑕丘鎮將，尋就拜東兗州刺史，改爵新泰侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Yan Province, and garrison commander at Xiaqiu; soon he was appointed in full as Governor of Eastern Yan Province and his title was changed to Marquis of Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Yan Province, and made garrison commander at Xiaqiu; shortly afterward he received formal appointment as Governor of Eastern Yan Province and his title was changed to Marquis of Xintai.

sentences.zh: 為政清平，新民樂附。

translations.literal: His administration was clear and even, and the new people were glad to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was fair and tranquil, and the newly settled population was glad to rally to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，入為給事中，遷儀曹長，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he entered the court as Gentlemen Attendant, was transferred to chief of the Bureau of Rites, and given the additional title Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he entered court service as Gentlemen Attendant, was promoted to chief of the Bureau of Rites, and given the additional title Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 清約恭謹，號為稱職。

translations.literal: Clear and frugal, respectful and cautious, he was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal, respectful, and cautious, he was widely regarded as thoroughly fit for his post.

sentences.zh: 後王師南討，詔假安南將軍、儀曹尚書、廣平公，與梁郡王嘉參謀軍計。

translations.literal: Later, when the royal army marched south on campaign, an edict made him acting General Who Pacifies the South, Minister of the Bureau of Rites, and Duke of Guangping, to join Prince Jia of Liang Commandery in planning military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the imperial army marched south on campaign, an edict appointed him acting General Who Pacifies the South, Minister of the Bureau of Rites, and Duke of Guangping, to join Prince Jia of Liang Commandery in planning the campaign.

sentences.zh: 後兗州民叛，詔明根慰喻。

translations.literal: Later, when the people of Yan Province rebelled, an edict ordered Minggen to comfort and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Yan Province later rose in revolt, an edict ordered Minggen to go and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 敕南征沔西、仇城、連口三道諸軍，[2]禀明根節度。

translations.literal: An order directed the three armies of the southern campaign on the west of the Mian, at Qiucheng, and at Liankou[2] to take their orders from Minggen.
translations.idiomatic: An order directed the three southern campaign forces west of the Mian, at Qiucheng, and at Liankou[2] to report to Minggen for command.

sentences.zh: 還都，正尚書，仍加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was made full Minister of the Palace Secretariat and again given the additional title Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he received formal appointment as Minister of the Palace Secretariat and again held the additional title Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 詔以與蕭賾絕使多年，今宜通否，羣臣會議。

translations.literal: An edict stated that diplomatic missions with Xiao Ze had been broken off for many years, and asked whether they should now be resumed; the ministers met to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that diplomatic contact with Xiao Ze had been suspended for many years and asked whether missions should now be resumed; the ministers were convened to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 尚書陸叡曰：「先以三吳不靖，荊梁有難，故權停之，將觀釁而動。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Rui said: "Previously, because the Three Wu were unsettled and Jing and Liang were in difficulty, we suspended missions for the time being, intending to watch for an opening and act.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Rui said, "We suspended missions earlier because the Three Wu were unsettled and Jing and Liang were in turmoil, intending to watch for an opening and act when the moment came.

sentences.zh: 今彼方既靖，宜還通使。」

translations.literal: Now that their side is settled, we should restore diplomatic missions."
translations.idiomatic: Now that their realm is calm, we ought to restore diplomatic contact."

sentences.zh: 明根曰：「中絕行人，是朝廷之事，深築醴陽，侵彼境土，二三之理，直在蕭賾。

translations.literal: Minggen said: "Cutting off envoys was the court's affair; building Liyang in depth and encroaching on their territory—the rights and wrongs of the matter lie squarely with Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen said, "Breaking off envoys was our court's decision; building up Liyang and encroaching on their territory—the rights and wrongs of the quarrel lie with Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 我今遣使，於理為長。」

translations.literal: If we now send envoys, we will be in the right by principle."
translations.idiomatic: If we send envoys now, we will stand on the stronger ground in principle."

sentences.zh: 高祖從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xiaowen followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 文明太后崩，羣臣固請公除，高祖與明根往復。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, the ministers firmly pressed for the termination of mourning in public service; the Emperor Xiaowen and Minggen exchanged arguments back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, the ministers repeatedly pressed for the emperor to end mourning and resume public duties; Emperor Xiaowen and Minggen debated the matter at length.

sentences.zh: 事在禮志。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 遷大鴻臚卿、河南王幹師，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Grand Reception and tutor to Prince Gan of Henan, while retaining his post as Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Grand Reception and appointed tutor to Prince Gan of Henan, while retaining his post as Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隨例降侯為伯。

translations.literal: In accordance with precedent his marquisate was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the usual reform, his marquisate was reduced to a barony.

sentences.zh: 又參定律令，屢進讜言。

translations.literal: He also took part in compiling statutes and ordinances and repeatedly offered forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in compiling statutes and ordinances and repeatedly offered candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 明根以年踰七十，表求致仕。

translations.literal: Minggen, his years having passed seventy, submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen, having passed seventy, submitted a memorial requesting retirement from office.

sentences.zh: 詔不許，頻表固請，乃詔曰：「明根風度清幹，志尚貞敏，溫恭靜密，乞言是寄，故抑其高蹈之操，至于再三。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it; he submitted memorials repeatedly and firmly requesting it, whereupon an edict said: "Minggen's bearing is clear and capable, his aims upright and keen, his manner warm, respectful, quiet, and thorough; we rely on him for counsel, and therefore restrained his lofty resolve to withdraw, down to the third time.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused permission; he submitted memorial after memorial insisting on retirement, whereupon an edict said, "Minggen's bearing is clear and capable, his aims upright and keen, his manner warm, respectful, quiet, and thorough. We rely on him for counsel, and therefore restrained his lofty resolve to withdraw—not once, but again and again.

sentences.zh: 表請殷勤，不容違奪，便已許其告辨。

translations.literal: His memorial requests were earnest and could not be denied; we have already granted his request to retire.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were so earnest that they could not be refused; we have already granted his request to retire.

sentences.zh: [3]可出前後表付外，依禮施行。」

translations.literal: [3] Let his earlier and later memorials be issued abroad and carried out according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: [3] Issue his earlier and later memorials abroad and carry out the retirement according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 引明根入見，高祖曰：「卿年耆德茂，服勤累朝，歷職內外，並著顯績，逮于耆老，履道不渝，是以釐革之始，委以禮任，遲能迂德，匡贊於朕。

translations.literal: He summoned Minggen to an audience. The Emperor Xiaowen said: "You are advanced in years and rich in virtue, diligent through many reigns; in posts within and without the court you have all shown outstanding achievement; reaching old age, you have not wavered from the Way. Therefore at the beginning of reform I entrusted you with ritual duties, deferring to your ability and lofty virtue to assist and support me.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Minggen to an audience. Emperor Xiaowen said, "You are advanced in years and rich in virtue, diligent through many reigns. In posts within and without the court alike you have achieved distinction; in old age you have not wavered from the Way. That is why, at the beginning of our reforms, I entrusted you with ritual duties, deferring to your ability and lofty character to assist and support me.

sentences.zh: 然高尚悠邈，便爾言歸，君臣之禮，於斯而畢，眷德思仁，情何可已。

translations.literal: Yet you are lofty and remote, and now speak of returning home; the rites between ruler and minister end here, yet my regard for your virtue and thought of your kindness—how can feeling cease?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hold yourself aloof and remote, and now speak of going home. The rites between ruler and minister end here, yet my regard for your virtue and memory of your kindness—how can my feeling cease?

sentences.zh: 夫七十致仕，典禮所稱；

translations.literal: Retirement at seventy is what the canonical rites commend;
translations.idiomatic: Retirement at seventy is what the canonical rites commend;

sentences.zh: 位隆固辭，賢者達節。

translations.literal: when rank is lofty yet one firmly declines, the worthy manifest their consummate integrity.
translations.idiomatic: when rank is high yet one firmly declines office, the worthy show their consummate integrity.

sentences.zh: 但季俗陵遲，斯道弗繼。

translations.literal: But in this declining age custom has decayed, and this Way is no longer continued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in this declining age custom has decayed, and this Way is scarcely practiced anymore.

sentences.zh: 卿獨秉冲操，居今行古，有魏以來，首振頹俗，進可以光我朝化，退可以榮慰私門。」

translations.literal: You alone hold to a pure integrity, practicing antiquity in the present age; since Wei began you are the first to revive a fallen custom—in advancing you can illumine our court's transformation, in withdrawing you can bring honor and comfort to your household."
translations.idiomatic: You alone hold to a pure integrity, practicing antiquity in the present age. Since the founding of Wei you are the first to revive a fallen custom—in advancing you can illumine our court's reforms, in withdrawing you can bring honor and comfort to your household."

sentences.zh: 明根對曰：「臣桑榆之年，鍾鳴漏盡，蒙陛下之澤，首領獲全，待盡私庭，下奉先帝陛下大恩，臣之願也。

translations.literal: Minggen replied: "Your servant is in the evening of life; the bell has sounded and the clepsydra is spent. I have received Your Majesty's grace and kept my person whole; to await my end in private quarters and below render the great kindness of the former emperor and Your Majesty—this is your servant's wish.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen replied, "Your servant is in the evening of life; the bell has sounded and the water-clock is spent. I have received Your Majesty's grace and kept body and life whole. To await my end at home and below render the great kindness of the former emperor and Your Majesty—that is your servant's wish.

sentences.zh: 但犬馬之戀，不勝悲塞。」

translations.literal: Yet the love of dog and horse cannot overcome grief that chokes the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the love of dog and horse cannot overcome the grief that chokes my heart."

sentences.zh: 因泣不自勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until he could no longer contain himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖命之令進，言別殷勤，仍為流涕。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xiaowen ordered him to advance; his parting words were earnest, and he too shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen ordered him to come forward; his parting words were warm and earnest, and the emperor too wept.

sentences.zh: 賜青紗單衣、委貌冠、被褥、錦袍等物。

translations.literal: He was granted a plain summer robe of green gauze, a weimao cap, bedding, a brocade robe, and other items.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a plain summer robe of green gauze, a weimao cap, bedding, a brocade robe, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 其年，以司徒尉元為三老，明根為五更，行禮辟雍。

translations.literal: That year, with Minister of Works Wei Yuan as the Sanlao and Minggen as the Wugeng, the rites were performed at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with Minister of Works Wei Yuan as Sanlao and Minggen as Wugeng, the ceremonial rites were performed at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 語在元傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Yuan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The account is given in Yuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 賜步挽一乘，給上卿之祿，供食之味，太官就第月送之。

translations.literal: He was granted one hand-drawn carriage, given the salary of a chief minister, and the flavors of the imperial table; the Imperial Kitchen sent them monthly to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hand-drawn carriage, given the salary of a chief minister, and provisions from the imperial table; the Imperial Kitchen delivered them monthly to his home.

sentences.zh: 以定律令之勤，賜布帛一千匹、穀一千斛。

translations.literal: For his diligence in compiling statutes and ordinances he was granted one thousand bolts of cloth and silk and one thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: For his diligence in compiling statutes and ordinances he was granted one thousand bolts of cloth and silk and one thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 後明根歸廣平，賜絹五百匹、安車一乘、馬二匹、幄帳被褥。

translations.literal: Later, when Minggen returned to Guangping, he was granted five hundred bolts of silk, one secure carriage, two horses, and curtains, bedding, and quilts.
translations.idiomatic: When Minggen later returned to Guangping, he was granted five hundred bolts of silk, one secure carriage, two horses, and curtains, bedding, and quilts.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸鄴，明根朝于行宮。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Ye, Minggen attended court at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Ye, Minggen presented himself at court in the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「游五更光素蓬簷，歸終衡里，可謂朝之舊德，國之老成。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You the Wugeng, plain and unadorned beneath a thatched eaves, ending your days in a lane of the capital district—you may be called an old virtue of the court and a seasoned pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "You the Wugeng, plain and unadorned beneath a thatched roof, ending your days in a humble lane—you are truly an old virtue of the court and a seasoned pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 可賜帛五百匹、穀五百斛。」

translations.literal: You may be granted five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him five hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 敕太官備送珍羞。

translations.literal: An order directed the Imperial Kitchen to prepare and send delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: An order directed the Imperial Kitchen to prepare and send delicacies.

sentences.zh: 後車駕幸鄴，又朝行宮，賜穀帛如前，為造甲第。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage again visited Ye, he again attended at the traveling palace and was granted grain and silk as before; a fine mansion was built for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later visited Ye again, Minggen again attended at the traveling palace and received grain and silk as before; a fine mansion was built for him.

sentences.zh: 國有大事，恒璽書訪之。

translations.literal: When the state had great affairs, the emperor invariably sent sealed edicts to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state faced great affairs, the emperor invariably sent sealed edicts to seek his counsel.

sentences.zh: 舊疹發動，手詔問疾，太醫送藥。

translations.literal: When an old ailment flared up, the emperor personally wrote to inquire after his illness, and the imperial physicians sent medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When an old ailment flared up, the emperor wrote in his own hand to inquire after his health, and the imperial physicians sent medicine.

sentences.zh: 太和二十三年卒於家，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Taihe he died at home, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Taihe he died at home, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣使弔祭，賻錢一十萬、絹三百匹、布二百匹，贈光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，諡靖侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu sent envoys to offer condolences; funeral gifts were one hundred thousand in cash, three hundred bolts of silk, and two hundred bolts of cloth. He was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu sent envoys to offer condolences; funeral gifts were one hundred thousand in cash, three hundred bolts of silk, and two hundred bolts of cloth. He was posthumously appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash, and given the posthumous title Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 明根歷官內外五十餘年，處身以仁和，接物以禮讓，時論貴之。

translations.literal: Minggen held office within and without the court for more than fifty years; he conducted himself with benevolence and harmony and treated others with ritual and deference, and opinion of the time prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen held office within and without the court for more than fifty years. He conducted himself with benevolence and harmony and treated others with courtesy and deference, and his contemporaries held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，明根與高閭以儒老學業，特被禮遇，公私出入，每相追隨，而閭以才筆時侮明根，世號高、游焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Minggen and Gao Lu, because of their learning in Confucian and classical studies, received special courtesy; in public and private they went in and out together and always followed one another, yet Lu with his literary talent sometimes slighted Minggen, and the age called them Gao and You.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Minggen and Gao Lu, for their learning in Confucian and classical studies, received special favor. In public and private they went in and out together and were seldom apart, yet Lu with his literary talent sometimes slighted Minggen, and the age called them Gao and You.

sentences.zh: 子肇襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 肇，字伯始，高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Zhao, styled Boshi, was given his name by the Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, whose courtesy name was Boshi, received his given name as a gift from Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 幼為中書學生，博通經史及蒼、雅、林說。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student at the Palace Secretariat school and mastered the classics and histories, as well as the Cangjie, Erya, and Forest of Sayings.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a student at the Palace Secretariat school and mastered the classics and histories, as well as lexicographical works such as the Cangjie, Erya, and Forest of Sayings.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，為內祕書侍御中散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as Attendant Cavalier in the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served as Attendant Cavalier in the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 司州初建，為都官從事，轉通直郎、祕閣令，遷散騎侍郎、典命中大夫。

translations.literal: When Si Province was first established he served as clerk in the Bureau of Justice, was transferred to Direct Attendant and Director of the Secret Archive, and was promoted to Attendant Cavalier and Grand Master in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Si Province was first established he served as clerk in the Bureau of Justice, was transferred to Direct Attendant and Director of the Secret Archive, and was promoted to Attendant Cavalier and Grand Master in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，肇上表諫止，高祖不納。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Zhao submitted a memorial remonstrating and urging halt; the Emperor Xiaowen did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zhao submitted a memorial urging him to stop; Emperor Xiaowen did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 肇謙素敦重，文雅見任。

translations.literal: Zhao was modest, plain, and solidly serious, and was entrusted for his literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was modest, plain, and solidly serious, and was entrusted for his literary refinement.

sentences.zh: 以父老，求解官扶侍。

translations.literal: Because his father was old, he requested to leave office to support and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was elderly, he asked to leave office to support and attend him.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲令遂祿養，乃出為本州南安王楨鎮北府長史，帶魏郡太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xiaowen wished him to continue receiving salary while supporting his father, and therefore sent him out as chief administrator of Prince Zhen of Nan'an's northern headquarters in his home province, concurrently serving as Governor of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen wished him to continue receiving salary while caring for his father, and therefore sent him out as chief administrator of Prince Zhen of Nan'an's northern headquarters in his home province, concurrently serving as Governor of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 王薨，復為高陽王雍鎮北府長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the prince died, he again became chief administrator of Prince Yong of Gaoyang's northern headquarters, with his governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died, he became chief administrator of Prince Yong of Gaoyang's northern headquarters, retaining his post as governor.

sentences.zh: 為政清簡，加以匡贊，歷佐二王，甚有聲迹。

translations.literal: His administration was clear and simple; moreover he assisted and supported his princes, and through serving two princes in succession he left a strong record of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was clear and unpretentious, and he assisted his princes effectively; through serving two princes in succession he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 數年，以父憂解任。

translations.literal: After several years he left office on account of mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 景明末，徵為廷尉少卿，固辭，乃授黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jingming era he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice; he firmly declined, and was then appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingming era he was summoned as Vice Minister of Justice; he firmly declined, and was then appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，黃門如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, with his Yellow Gate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary while retaining his post at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 兼侍中，為畿內大使，黜陟善惡，賞罰分明。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and served as envoy within the capital region, promoting and demoting good and bad, with rewards and punishments clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and served as envoy within the capital region, promoting and demoting the worthy and unworthy with clear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 轉太府卿，徙廷尉卿，兼御史中尉，黃門如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Treasury, moved to Minister of Justice, and concurrently made Imperial Censor, with his Yellow Gate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Treasury, then to Minister of Justice, and concurrently appointed Imperial Censor, while retaining his post at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 肇，儒者，動存名教，直繩所舉，莫非傷風敗俗。

translations.literal: Zhao, a Confucian, in action upheld the norms of teaching; whatever the straight cord of law raised up was never other than conduct that injured custom and corrupted morals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, a Confucian scholar, in all his actions upheld the norms of moral teaching; every case he brought forward under the law concerned conduct that offended custom and corrupted public morals.

sentences.zh: 持法仁平，斷獄務於矜恕。

translations.literal: He held the law with benevolence and fairness, and in judging cases strove for compassionate forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law with benevolence and fairness, and in judging cases strove for compassionate forbearance.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇，世宗之舅，為百僚懾憚，以肇名與己同，欲令改易。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, Minister of Works and the maternal uncle of Emperor Xuanwu, was feared by all officials; because Zhao's name was the same as his own, he wished him to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Minister of Works and maternal uncle of Emperor Xuanwu, was feared by all officials. Because Zhao's name was the same as his own, he wanted Zhao to change it.

sentences.zh: 肇以高祖所賜，秉志不許，高肇甚銜之。

translations.literal: Zhao, because it was a name given by the Emperor Xiaowen, held to his resolve and would not agree; Gao Zhao bore a deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, because it was a name given by Emperor Xiaowen, held firm and refused; Gao Zhao deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉其剛梗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu praised his firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu praised his firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 盧昶之在朐山也，肇諫曰：「朐山蕞爾，僻在海濱，山湖下墊，民無居者，於我非急，於賊為利。

translations.literal: When Lu Chang was at Qushan, Zhao remonstrated: "Qushan is tiny, remote on the seacoast; mountains and lakes lie low, and the people have no place to dwell. For us it is not urgent; for the enemy it is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Chang was at Qushan, Zhao remonstrated, "Qushan is tiny and remote on the seacoast; mountains and lakes lie low, and the people have nowhere to live. For us it is not urgent; for the enemy it is advantageous.

sentences.zh: 為利，故必致死而爭之；

translations.literal: Because it is advantageous, they will certainly fight to the death for it;
translations.idiomatic: Because it is advantageous, they will certainly fight to the death for it;

sentences.zh: 非急，故不得已而戰。

translations.literal: because it is not urgent for us, we fight only when we have no choice.
translations.idiomatic: because it is not urgent for us, we fight only when we have no choice.

sentences.zh: 以不得已之眾，擊必死之師，恐稽延歲月，所費遂甚。

translations.literal: To pit troops who fight only because they must against an army that will certainly die— I fear months will drag on and the cost will become very great.
translations.idiomatic: To pit troops who fight only because they must against an army resolved to die—I fear the campaign will drag on for months and the cost will become very great.

sentences.zh: 假令必得朐山，徒致交爭，終難全守，所謂無益之田也。

translations.literal: Even if we were certain to take Qushan, we would only provoke mutual contention and in the end could scarcely hold it secure—it is what is called useless land.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we were certain to take Qushan, we would only provoke endless contention and could scarcely hold it in the end—it is what people call useless land.

sentences.zh: 知賊將屢以宿豫求易朐山，臣愚謂此言可許。

translations.literal: Knowing that the enemy has repeatedly offered to exchange Suyu for Qushan, your servant in his folly thinks this proposal may be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that the enemy has repeatedly offered to exchange Suyu for Qushan, your servant in his folly thinks this proposal should be accepted.

sentences.zh: 朐山久捍危弊，宜速審之。

translations.literal: Qushan has long been defended in peril and exhaustion; it should quickly be reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Qushan has long been defended in peril and exhaustion; the matter should be reconsidered at once.

sentences.zh: 若必如此，宿豫不征而自伏。

translations.literal: If this is done, Suyu will submit without our having to campaign for it.
translations.idiomatic: If this is done, Suyu will submit without our having to campaign for it.

sentences.zh: 持此無用之地，復彼舊有之疆，兵役時解，其利為大。」

translations.literal: Holding this useless place while recovering their former territory, the military service will soon be ended—its benefit would be great."
translations.idiomatic: Giving up this useless place while recovering territory they once held, we would soon end the campaign— the benefit would be great."

sentences.zh: 世宗將從之，尋而昶敗。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu was about to follow his advice, but soon afterward Chang was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu was about to follow his advice, but soon afterward Chang was defeated.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍軍主徐玄明斬其青冀二州刺史張稷首，以郁洲內附，朝議遣兵赴援。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's army commander Xu Xuanming beheaded Zhang Ji, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, and offered Yuzhou in submission; the court debated sending troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's army commander Xu Xuanming beheaded Zhang Ji, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, and offered Yuzhou in submission; the court debated sending troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 肇表曰：「玄明之款，雖奔救是當，然事有損益，或憚舉而功多，或因小而生患，不可必也。

translations.literal: Zhao submitted a memorial: "Xuanming's submission, though a rescue mission would be appropriate, yet affairs have gain and loss; sometimes one fears to act yet the achievement is great, sometimes one acts on a small matter and great trouble arises—nothing is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao submitted a memorial saying, "Xuanming's submission, though a rescue mission would be appropriate, yet affairs have their gains and losses; sometimes one hesitates to act yet the achievement proves great, sometimes one acts on a small matter and great trouble follows—nothing is certain.

sentences.zh: 今六里、朐山，地實接海，陂湖下濕，人不可居。

translations.literal: Now Liuli and Qushan—their lands truly border the sea; marshes and lakes lie low and wet, and people cannot dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Liuli and Qushan today truly border the sea; marshes and lakes lie low and wet, and people cannot live there.

sentences.zh: 郁洲又在海中，所謂雖獲石田，終無所用。

translations.literal: Yuzhou is again in the sea; it is what is called gaining stony fields that in the end are of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou lies in the sea as well; it is what people call gaining stony fields that in the end are of no use.

sentences.zh: 若不得連口，六里雖克，尚不可守，況方事連兵，而爭非要也。

translations.literal: If Liankou is not taken, even if Liuli is captured it still cannot be held; how much more when we are already engaged in continuous warfare yet contend for what is not essential.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not take Liankou, even capturing Liuli will not make it tenable—and all the more so when we are already fighting continuously yet striving for what is not essential.

sentences.zh: 且六里於賊逾要，去此閑遠。

translations.literal: Moreover Liuli is all the more vital to the enemy and lies far from our idle rear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liuli is all the more vital to the enemy and lies far from our secure rear.

sentences.zh: 若以閑遠之兵，攻逼近之眾，其勢既殊，不可敵也。

translations.literal: If troops from a distant and idle region attack a nearby mass of the enemy, the disparity of circumstance is such that they cannot be matched.
translations.idiomatic: If troops from a distant rear attack an enemy mass close at hand, the disparity of strength is such that they cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 災儉之年，百姓飢弊，餓死者亦復不少。

translations.literal: In a year of disaster and scarcity the common people are hungry and exhausted, and those who die of starvation are again not a few.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of disaster and scarcity the common people are hungry and exhausted, and many die of starvation besides.

sentences.zh: 何以得宜靜之辰，興干戈之役？

translations.literal: How can we find a time fit for tranquillity and raise the business of war?
translations.idiomatic: How can we find a moment fit for tranquillity and yet raise the business of war?

sentences.zh: 軍糧資運，取濟無所。

translations.literal: Army grain and transport supplies have nowhere from which to draw support.
translations.idiomatic: Army grain and transport supplies have nowhere from which to draw support.

sentences.zh: 唯見其損，未覩其益。

translations.literal: We see only the harm and do not see the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: We see only the harm and do not see the benefit.

sentences.zh: 且新附之民，服化猶近，特須安帖，不宜勞之。

translations.literal: Moreover the newly submitted people have only lately accepted our rule; they especially need reassurance and should not be wearied.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the newly submitted people have only lately accepted our rule; they especially need reassurance and should not be wearied.

sentences.zh: 勞則怨生，怨生則思叛，思叛則不自安，不安則擾動。

translations.literal: If they are wearied, resentment arises; if resentment arises, they think of rebellion; if they think of rebellion, they are not at ease; if they are not at ease, disturbance follows.
translations.idiomatic: If they are wearied, resentment arises; resentment breeds thoughts of rebellion; rebellion breeds insecurity; insecurity breeds unrest.

sentences.zh: 脫爾，則連兵難解。

translations.literal: If it comes to that, continuous warfare will be hard to end.
translations.idiomatic: If it comes to that, continuous warfare will be hard to end.

sentences.zh: 事不可輕。

translations.literal: The matter must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The matter must not be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 宜損茲小利，不使大損。」

translations.literal: We should forgo this small gain so as not to suffer a great loss.
translations.idiomatic: We should forgo this small gain so as not to suffer a great loss.

sentences.zh: 世宗並不納。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 大將軍高肇伐蜀，肇諫曰：「臣聞：遠人不服，則修文德以來之。

translations.literal: When the General-in-Chief Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Zhao remonstrated: "Your servant has heard: when distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: When General-in-Chief Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Zhao remonstrated, "Your servant has heard that when distant peoples do not submit, one should cultivate civil virtue to draw them in.

sentences.zh: 兵者凶器，不得已而後用。

translations.literal: Arms are inauspicious instruments, used only when there is no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are inauspicious instruments, used only when there is no alternative.

sentences.zh: 當今治雖太平，論征未可。

translations.literal: Although governance today is largely at peace, to speak of campaigning is not yet permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Although governance today is largely at peace, to speak of campaigning is not yet permissible.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 山東、關右，殘傷未復，頻年水旱，百姓空虛，宜在安靜，不宜勞役。

translations.literal: East of the mountains and west of the passes, wounds from past disasters have not yet healed; year after year of flood and drought have left the people empty and destitute—they should be kept in tranquillity, not wearied with corvée.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountains and west of the passes, wounds from past disasters have not yet healed; year after year of flood and drought have left the people empty and destitute—they should be kept in tranquillity, not wearied with corvée.

sentences.zh: 然往昔開拓，皆因城主歸款，故有征無戰。

translations.literal: Yet in past expansion, it was always because city lords submitted in good faith, and therefore there were campaigns without battles.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in past expansion, it was always because city lords submitted in good faith, and therefore there were campaigns without battles.

sentences.zh: 今之據者，[4]雖假官號，真偽難分，或有怨於彼，不可全信。

translations.literal: Those who hold territory today,[4] though they borrow official titles, are hard to distinguish true from false; some may bear grievances against them and cannot be wholly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold territory today,[4] though they borrow official titles, are hard to distinguish true from false; some may bear grievances against them and cannot be wholly trusted.

sentences.zh: 且蜀地險隘，稱之自古，鎮戍晏然，更無異趣，豈得虛承浮說，而動大軍。

translations.literal: Moreover Shu terrain is perilous and narrow, as it has been called since antiquity; garrisons are tranquil and show no other inclination—how can we move a great army on empty floating talk?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shu terrain is perilous and narrow, as it has been called since antiquity; garrisons are tranquil and show no other inclination—how can we move a great army on empty floating talk?

sentences.zh: 舉不慎始，悔將何及！

translations.literal: If one is not careful at the start, what regret will there be afterward!
translations.idiomatic: If one is not careful at the start, what regret will there be afterward!

sentences.zh: 討蜀之略，願俟後圖。」

translations.literal: The plan to attack Shu—I beg that it await a later design.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to attack Shu—I beg that it await a later design.

sentences.zh: 世宗又不納。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu again did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu again did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，遷中書令、光祿大夫，加金章紫綬，相州大中正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zhao was promoted to Palace Secretary, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash, and Chief Rectifier of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Zhao was promoted to Palace Secretary and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with golden seal and purple sash, and made Chief Rectifier of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節，加散騎常侍、鎮東將軍、相州刺史，有惠政。

translations.literal: He went out bearing the staff of office, with the additional titles Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the East, and as Governor of Xiang Province his administration was benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing the staff of office, with the additional titles Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and General Who Pacifies the East, and as Governor of Xiang Province his administration was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 徵為太常卿，遷尚書右僕射，固辭，詔不許。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies, promoted to Vice Minister of the Left in the Palace Secretariat, firmly declined, and an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Minister of Ceremonies, promoted to Vice Minister of the Left in the Palace Secretariat, firmly declined, and an edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 肇於吏事，斷決不速。

translations.literal: In administrative matters Zhao was not swift in deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: In administrative matters Zhao was not swift in deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 主者諮呈，反覆論叙，有時不曉，至於再三，必窮其理，然後下筆，雖寵勢干請，終無回撓。

translations.literal: When superiors presented matters for consultation, he would argue back and forth; sometimes he did not understand at once, and would go to a third round, always exhausting the principle before putting brush to paper; even when favored power intervened with requests, in the end he would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: When superiors presented matters for consultation, he would argue back and forth; sometimes he did not understand at once and would go to a third round, always exhausting the principle before putting brush to paper; even when favored power intervened with requests, in the end he would not bend.

sentences.zh: 方正之操，時人服之。

translations.literal: His upright integrity was what men of the time admired.
translations.idiomatic: His upright integrity was what men of the time admired.

sentences.zh: 及領軍元叉之廢靈太后，將害太傅、清河王懌，乃集公卿會議其事。

translations.literal: When the commander Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling and was about to harm the Grand Tutor, Prince Yi of Qinghe, he gathered the ministers to deliberate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the commander Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling and was about to harm the Grand Tutor, Prince Yi of Qinghe, he gathered the ministers to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 於時羣官莫不失色順旨，肇獨抗言以為不可，終不下署。

translations.literal: At that time none of the officials failed to lose color and follow his intent; Zhao alone spoke against it and in the end would not sign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time none of the officials failed to lose color and follow his intent; Zhao alone spoke against it and in the end would not sign.

sentences.zh: 正光元年八月卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhengguang he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhengguang he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 詔給東園祕器、朝服一襲，賵帛七百匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted the eastern garden funerary vessels and one set of court robes, with funeral gifts of seven hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the eastern garden funerary vessels and one set of court robes, with funeral gifts of seven hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 肅宗舉哀於朝堂。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong offered mourning in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong offered mourning in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the staff of office, Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, ritual parity with the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the staff of office, Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, ritual parity with the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 肇外寬柔，內剛直，耽好經傳，手不釋書。

translations.literal: Outwardly Zhao was gentle and yielding, inwardly firm and upright; he delighted in the classics and never let books leave his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was gentle and yielding, inwardly firm and upright; he delighted in the classics and never let books leave his hands.

sentences.zh: 治周易、毛詩，尤精三禮。

translations.literal: He studied the Changes and the Mao version of the Odes, and was especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Changes and the Mao version of the Odes, and was especially expert in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 為易集解，撰冠婚儀、白珪論，詩賦表啟凡七十五篇，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: He compiled an exegesis of the Changes, wrote treatises on capping and marriage rites and on the white jade disc, and in all seventy-five pieces of poetry, rhapsodies, memorials, and letters, all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled an exegesis of the Changes, wrote treatises on capping and marriage rites and on the white jade disc, and in all seventy-five pieces of poetry, rhapsodies, memorials, and letters, all of which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 謙廉不競，曾撰儒碁，以表其志焉。

translations.literal: Humble and uncontentious, he once composed a Confucian chess game to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and uncontentious, he once composed a Confucian chess game to express his intent.

sentences.zh: 清貧寡欲，資仰俸祿而已。

translations.literal: Pure and poor, with few desires—he relied on his official salary and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in austere poverty with few desires, relying on his official salary and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 肇之為廷尉也，世宗嘗私敕肇，有所降恕。

translations.literal: When Zhao served as Minister of Justice, Emperor Xuanwu once privately instructed Zhao to show leniency in certain cases.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao served as Minister of Justice, Emperor Xuanwu once privately instructed him to show leniency in certain cases.

sentences.zh: 肇執而不從，曰：「陛下自能恕之，豈足令臣曲筆也！」

translations.literal: Zhao held firm and did not comply, saying: "Your Majesty can pardon them on your own—how could that suffice to make your servant distort the record!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao held firm and refused, saying: "Your Majesty can pardon them on your own—how could that suffice to make me distort the record!"

sentences.zh: 其執意如此。

translations.literal: Such was the firmness of his conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the firmness of his conviction.

sentences.zh: 及肅宗初，近侍羣官豫在奉迎者，自侍中崔光已下並加封邑，時封肇文安縣開國侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong first ascended, the close attendants and officials who had taken part in welcoming him, from Palace Attendant Cui Guang downward, all received enfeoffments; at that time Zhao was enfeoffed as founding marquis of Wen'an County with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong first ascended, the close attendants and officials who had taken part in welcoming him, from Palace Attendant Cui Guang downward, all received enfeoffments; at that time Zhao was enfeoffed as founding marquis of Wen'an County with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 肇獨曰：「子襲父位，今古之常，因此獲封，何以自處？」

translations.literal: Zhao alone said: "A son inherits his father's position—this is the constant practice from antiquity to the present; to receive enfeoffment on this account, how could one comport oneself?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao alone said: "A son inherits his father's position—this is the constant practice from antiquity to the present; to receive enfeoffment on this account, how could one comport oneself?"

sentences.zh: 固辭不應。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 論者高之。

translations.literal: Commentators esteemed him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators esteemed him for it.

sentences.zh: 子祥，字宗良，頗有學。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, courtesy name Zongliang, was quite learned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, courtesy name Zongliang, was quite learned.

sentences.zh: 歷祕書郎，襲爵新泰伯。

translations.literal: He served as Secretary in the Palace Library and inherited the title Baron of Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretary in the Palace Library and inherited the title Baron of Xintai.

sentences.zh: 遷通直郎、國子博士，領尚書郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Attendant and Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and concurrently served as Bureau Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant and Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and concurrently served as Bureau Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以肇昔辭文安之封，復欲封祥，祥守其父意，卒亦不受。

translations.literal: Because Zhao had once declined the Wen'an enfeoffment, Emperor Suzong wished again to enfeoff Xiang; Xiang upheld his father's intent and in the end likewise did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhao had once declined the Wen'an enfeoffment, Emperor Suzong wished again to enfeoff Xiang; Xiang upheld his father's intent and in the end likewise refused.

sentences.zh: 又追論肇前議清河，守正不屈，乃封祥高邑縣開國侯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: Moreover, recalling Zhao's earlier remonstrance concerning Qinghe and his upright refusal to yield, they enfeoffed Xiang as founding marquis of Gaoyi County with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, recalling Zhao's earlier remonstrance concerning Qinghe and his upright refusal to yield, they enfeoffed Xiang as founding marquis of Gaoyi County with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang he died, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、給事黃門侍郎、幽州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子皓，字賓多，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hao, courtesy name Binduo, succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao, courtesy name Binduo, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 侍御史。

translations.literal: Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 皓弟安居，襲爵新泰伯。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Anju inherited the title Baron of Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Anju inherited the title Baron of Xintai.

sentences.zh: 武定中，司空墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: During the Wuding era he served as Adjunct in the Ink Office of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as Adjunct in the Ink Office of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 明根叔父矯，中書博士，濮陽、鉅鹿二郡太守。

translations.literal: Minggen's paternal uncle Jiao served as Erudite of the Palace Secretariat and as Administrator of the two commanderies of Puyang and Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Minggen's paternal uncle Jiao served as Erudite of the Palace Secretariat and as Administrator of the two commanderies of Puyang and Julu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously granted General Who Conquers the Champions and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted General Who Conquers the Champions and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 矯孫馥，國子博士。

translations.literal: Jiao's grandson Fu was Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's grandson Fu was Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 馥弟思進，尚書郎中。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Sijin was Bureau Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Sijin was Bureau Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉芳，字伯文，彭城人也，漢楚元王之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, courtesy name Bowen, was a man of Pengcheng and a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, courtesy name Bowen, was a man of Pengcheng and a descendant of Prince Yuan of Chu of Han.

sentences.zh: 六世祖訥，晉司隸校尉。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Ne was Metropolitan Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Ne was Metropolitan Commandant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖該，劉義隆征虜將軍、青徐二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gai was General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Liu Yilong and Governor of the two provinces of Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gai was General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Liu Yilong and Governor of the two provinces of Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 父邕，劉駿兗州長史。

translations.literal: His father Yong was Chief Administrator of Yan Province under Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong was Chief Administrator of Yan Province under Liu Jun.

sentences.zh: 芳出後伯父遜之，遜之，劉駿東平太守也。

translations.literal: Fang was adopted to succeed his paternal uncle Xunzhi; Xunzhi was Administrator of Dongping under Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was adopted to succeed his paternal uncle Xunzhi; Xunzhi was Administrator of Dongping under Liu Jun.

sentences.zh: 邕同劉義宣之事，身死彭城。

translations.literal: Yong took part in Liu Yixuan's affair and died at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong took part in Liu Yixuan's affair and died at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 芳隨伯母房逃竄青州，會赦免。

translations.literal: Fang fled with his uncle's wife, née Fang, to Qing Province and was pardoned by an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fled with his uncle's wife, née Fang, to Qing Province and was pardoned by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 舅元慶，為劉子業青州刺史沈文秀建威府司馬，為文秀所殺。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle Yuanqing served as Military Administrator on the staff of the Establishing Might Office of Shen Wenxiu, Governor of Qing Province under Liu Ziye, and was killed by Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal uncle Yuanqing served as Military Administrator on the staff of the Establishing Might Office of Shen Wenxiu, Governor of Qing Province under Liu Ziye, and was killed by Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 芳母子入梁鄒城。

translations.literal: Fang and his mother entered Liangzou city.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and his mother entered Liangzou city.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜南討青齊，梁鄒降，芳北徙為平齊民，時年十六。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao marched south to subdue Qing and Qi, Liangzou surrendered, and Fang was relocated north as a subject pacified from Qi; he was then sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao marched south to subdue Qing and Qi, Liangzou surrendered, and Fang was relocated north as a subject pacified from Qi; he was then sixteen.

sentences.zh: 南部尚書李敷妻，司徒崔浩之弟女；

translations.literal: Li Fu, Minister of the Southern Branch, had a wife who was the daughter of Minister of Works Cui Hao's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, Minister of the Southern Branch, had a wife who was the daughter of Minister of Works Cui Hao's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 芳祖母，浩之姑也。

translations.literal: Fang's paternal grandmother was Hao's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's paternal grandmother was Hao's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 芳至京師，詣敷門，崔耻芳流播，拒不見之。

translations.literal: When Fang reached the capital and called at Fu's gate, the Cui clan, ashamed of Fang's wandering exile, refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang reached the capital and called at Fu's gate, the Cui clan, ashamed of Fang's wandering exile, refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 芳雖處窮窘之中，而業尚貞固，聰敏過人，篤志墳典。

translations.literal: Though Fang was in destitute straits, he still upheld rectitude and steadfastness, was clever beyond others, and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Though Fang was in destitute straits, he still upheld rectitude and steadfastness, was clever beyond others, and devoted himself wholeheartedly to the classics.

sentences.zh: 晝則傭書，以自資給，夜則讀誦，終夕不寢，至有易衣併日之弊，而澹然自守，不汲汲於榮利，不慼慼於賤貧，乃著窮通論以自慰焉。

translations.literal: By day he hired out his brush to support himself; by night he read and recited without sleeping the whole night through, until he would even change clothes only every other day—yet he remained calmly self-restrained, neither eager for honor and profit nor grieved at lowly poverty, and so wrote the Discourse on Adversity and Success to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: By day he hired out his brush to support himself; by night he read and recited without sleeping the whole night through, until he would even change clothes only every other day—yet he remained calmly self-restrained, neither eager for honor and profit nor grieved at lowly poverty, and so wrote the Discourse on Adversity and Success to console himself.

sentences.zh: 芳常為諸僧傭寫經論，筆迹稱善，卷直以一縑，歲中能入百餘匹，如此數十年，[5]賴以頗振。

translations.literal: Fang often wrote scriptures and treatises for monks for hire; his handwriting was praised, and he charged one bolt of silk per scroll—within a year he could earn more than a hundred bolts; for several decades on end,[5] by this means he came to live in modest comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Fang often wrote scriptures and treatises for monks for hire; his handwriting was praised, and he charged one bolt of silk per scroll—within a year he could earn more than a hundred bolts; for several decades on end,[5] by this means he came to live in modest comfort.

sentences.zh: 由是與德學大僧，多有還往。

translations.literal: Through this he came to have much association with eminent monks of virtue and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Through this he came to have much association with eminent monks of virtue and learning.

sentences.zh: 時有南方沙門惠度以事被責，未幾暴亡，芳因緣關知，文明太后召入禁中，鞭之一百。

translations.literal: At the time the southern monk Huidu was reprimanded over some affair and soon died suddenly; Fang was implicated through association, and Empress Dowager Wenming summoned him into the inner palace and had him flogged one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the southern monk Huidu was reprimanded over some affair and soon died suddenly; Fang was implicated through association, and Empress Dowager Wenming summoned him into the inner palace and had him flogged one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 時中官李豐主其始末，知芳篤學有志行，言之於太后，太后微愧於心。

translations.literal: At the time the palace eunuch Li Feng presided over the investigation; knowing Fang's devoted scholarship and worthy conduct, he spoke of it to the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager felt a slight shame at heart.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace eunuch Li Feng presided over the investigation; knowing Fang's devoted scholarship and worthy conduct, he spoke of it to the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager felt a slight shame at heart.

sentences.zh: 會蕭賾使劉纘至，芳之族兄也，擢芳兼主客郎，與纘相接。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiao Ze's envoy Liu Zuan arrived—Fang's clansman elder brother—and Fang was promoted to Acting Director of the Host and Guest Bureau to receive Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Xiao Ze's envoy Liu Zuan arrived—Fang's clansman elder brother—and Fang was promoted to Acting Director of the Host and Guest Bureau to receive Zuan.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Erudite of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Erudite of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後與崔光、宋弁、邢產等俱為中書侍郎，俄而詔芳與產入授皇太子經，遷太子庶子、兼員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he served together with Cui Guang, Song Bian, Xing Chan, and others as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; presently an edict ordered Fang and Chan to enter and instruct the Crown Prince in the classics; he was promoted to Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served together with Cui Guang, Song Bian, Xing Chan, and others as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; presently an edict ordered Fang and Chan to enter and instruct the Crown Prince in the classics; he was promoted to Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment.

sentences.zh: 從駕洛陽，自在路及旋京師，恒侍坐講讀。

translations.literal: When he accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, from the journey onward and upon return to the capital, he constantly attended at seat to lecture and read.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, from the journey onward and upon return to the capital, he constantly attended at seat to lecture and read.

sentences.zh: 芳才思深敏，特精經義，博聞強記，兼覽蒼、雅，尤長音訓，辨析無疑。

translations.literal: Fang's talent and thought were deeply sharp; he was especially skilled in the meaning of the classics, broadly learned with a strong memory, and also read the Cangjie and Erya lexicons; he was especially accomplished in pronunciation and glosses, and in discrimination left no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's talent and thought were deeply sharp; he was especially skilled in the meaning of the classics, broadly learned with a strong memory, and also read the Cangjie and Erya lexicons; he was especially accomplished in pronunciation and glosses, and in discrimination left no doubt.

sentences.zh: 於是禮遇日隆，賞賚豐渥，正除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Thereupon his ceremonial treatment grew daily more exalted and his rewards and gifts more abundant; he was formally appointed Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his ceremonial treatment grew daily more exalted and his rewards and gifts more abundant; he was formally appointed Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Outside the Regular Establishment.

sentences.zh: 俄兼通直常侍，從駕南巡，撰述行事，尋而除正。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he additionally served as Direct Transmission Attendant Cavalier; accompanying the imperial procession on the southern tour, he compiled an account of the journey; shortly afterward he was appointed to the regular post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he additionally served as Direct Transmission Attendant Cavalier; accompanying the imperial procession on the southern tour, he compiled an account of the journey; shortly afterward he was appointed to the regular post.

sentences.zh: 王肅之來奔也，高祖雅相器重，朝野屬目。

translations.literal: When Wang Su came over in flight, Emperor Xiaowen highly valued and esteemed him, and court and country fixed their eyes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su came over in flight, Emperor Xiaowen highly valued and esteemed him, and court and country fixed their eyes upon him.

sentences.zh: 芳未及相見。

translations.literal: Fang had not yet met him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had not yet met him.

sentences.zh: 高祖宴羣臣於華林，肅語次云「古者唯婦人有笄，男子則無」。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen feasted the ministers at Hualin Park; in the course of conversation Su said, "In antiquity only women had hairpins; men had none."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen feasted the ministers at Hualin Park; in the course of conversation Su said, "In antiquity only women had hairpins; men had none."

sentences.zh: 芳曰：「推經禮正文，古者男子婦人俱有笄。」

translations.literal: Fang said: "If one extrapolates from the canonical passages of ritual texts, in antiquity both men and women had hairpins."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said: "If one extrapolates from the canonical passages of ritual texts, in antiquity both men and women had hairpins."

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「喪服稱男子免而婦人髽，男子冠而婦人笄。

translations.literal: Su said: "The Mourning Dress [Classic] says: when the man ties up his hair, the woman binds hers in a topknot; when the man puts on his cap, the woman uses a hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: Su said: "The Mourning Dress [Classic] says: when the man ties up his hair, the woman binds hers in a topknot; when the man puts on his cap, the woman uses a hairpin.

sentences.zh: 如此，則男子不應有笄。」

translations.literal: In that case, men ought not to have hairpins."
translations.idiomatic: In that case, men ought not to have hairpins."

sentences.zh: 芳曰：「此專謂凶事也。

translations.literal: Fang said: "This refers specifically to inauspicious affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fang said: "This refers specifically to inauspicious affairs.

sentences.zh: 禮：初遭喪，男子免，時則婦人髽；

translations.literal: The rites say: at first encountering mourning, the man ties up his hair, and at that time the woman binds hers in a topknot;
translations.idiomatic: The rites say: at first encountering mourning, the man ties up his hair, and at that time the woman binds hers in a topknot;

sentences.zh: 男子冠，時則婦人笄。

translations.literal: when the man puts on his cap, at that time the woman uses a hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: when the man puts on his cap, at that time the woman uses a hairpin.

sentences.zh: 言俱時變，而男子婦人免髽、冠笄之不同也。

translations.literal: It means both change with the occasion, yet the differences between men and women in tying up the hair versus topknots, and cap versus hairpin, [are as stated].
translations.idiomatic: The passage means that both change according to the occasion—the manner in which men and women differ in hair-tying, topknots, caps, and hairpins.

sentences.zh: 又冠尊，故奪其笄稱。

translations.literal: Again, the cap is esteemed, so the hairpin [term] is suppressed in naming.
translations.idiomatic: Because the cap ranks higher, the text suppresses mention of the hairpin.

sentences.zh: 且互言也，非謂男子無笄。

translations.literal: Moreover it speaks of each in turn—it does not mean that men had no hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: The phrases refer to each sex in turn; they do not imply that men lacked hairpins.

sentences.zh: 又禮內則稱：『子事父母，雞初鳴，櫛纚笄總。』

translations.literal: Again, the Inner Canon of the Rites states: "When the son serves his parents, at the cock's first crow, he combs, binds, hairpins, and ties [his hair]."
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Canon of the Rites also says: "When a son attends to his parents, at the first crow of the cock he combs his hair, binds it, pins it, and ties it up."

sentences.zh: 以茲而言，男子有笄明矣。」

translations.literal: From this it is spoken—clearly men had hairpins."
translations.idiomatic: On this evidence, it is plain that men wore hairpins."

sentences.zh: 高祖稱善者久之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor praised [it] as good for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor expressed his approval at length.

sentences.zh: 肅亦以芳言為然，曰：「此非劉石經邪？」

translations.literal: Su also took Fang's words as correct, saying: "Is this not Liu the Stone Classics?"
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed with Fang and said: "Are you not Liu the Stone Classics?"

sentences.zh: 昔漢世造三字石經於太學，學者文字不正，多往質焉。

translations.literal: In former times during the Han, the Three-Script Stone Classics were carved at the Imperial Academy; scholars whose characters were incorrect often went to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the Three-Script Stone Classics had been erected at the Imperial Academy; when scholars found their texts corrupt, many went to him for correction.

sentences.zh: 芳音義明辨，疑者皆往詢訪，故時人號為劉石經。

translations.literal: Fang's pronunciation and meaning were clear and discerning; those in doubt all went to inquire, so people of the time called him Liu the Stone Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's readings and glosses were lucid; the perplexed came to him for answers, and contemporaries nicknamed him Liu the Stone Classics.

sentences.zh: 酒闌，芳與肅俱出，肅執芳手曰：「吾少來留意三禮，在南諸儒，亟共討論，皆謂此義如吾向言，今聞往釋，頓袪平生之惑。」

translations.literal: When the wine was nearly finished, Fang and Su both went out; Su took Fang's hand and said: "From my youth I have attended to the Three Rites; with the southern scholars I have often discussed them together, and all held this meaning as I had said before—now hearing your past explanation, I have suddenly cleared away a lifetime's confusion."
translations.idiomatic: As the feast drew to a close, Fang and Su left together. Su grasped Fang's hand and said: "Since youth I have studied the Three Rites. I debated them repeatedly with the southern scholars, and all confirmed my earlier view—but hearing your explanation just now has lifted a lifetime's uncertainty."

sentences.zh: 芳理義精通，類皆如是。

translations.literal: Fang's mastery of principles and meanings was thorough; cases were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's command of ritual doctrine was such across the board.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷洛，路由朝歌，見殷比干墓，愴然悼懷，為文以弔之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved to Luoyang, the route passed through Zhaoge; seeing the tomb of Yin Bigan, he sorrowfully mourned and wrote a composition to lament him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, his route passed through Zhaoge. Seeing the tomb of Yin Bigan, he was moved to sorrow and wrote a lament for him.

sentences.zh: 芳為注解，表上之。

translations.literal: Fang made annotations and explanations for it and submitted them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Fang annotated the piece and submitted his notes to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「覽卿注，殊為富博。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Looking over your annotations, they are especially rich and broad.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Reading your annotations, I find them exceptionally rich and wide-ranging.

sentences.zh: 但文非屈宋，理慚張賈。

translations.literal: But the writing is not Qu Yuan or Song Yu, and the reasoning falls short of Zhang and Jia.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the composition is no Qu Yuan or Song Yu, and its argument falls short of Zhang and Jia.

sentences.zh: 既有雅致，便可付之集書。」

translations.literal: Since it has refined elegance, it may be entrusted to the collected writings."
translations.idiomatic: Since it nevertheless has refined elegance, it may be placed among the collected writings."

sentences.zh: 詔以芳經學精洽，超遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: By edict, because Fang's classical learning was precise and comprehensive, he was promoted beyond the normal sequence to Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fang's command of the classics was exact and thorough, the emperor promoted him out of turn to Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office because of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖南征宛鄧，起為輔國將軍、太尉長史，從太尉、咸陽王禧攻南陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south against Wan and Deng, Fang was raised to serve as General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, and accompanied the Grand Commandant, Prince Xi of Xianyang, in attacking Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south against Wan and Deng, Fang was recalled as General Who Assists the State and Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, accompanying Prince Xi of Xianyang, the Grand Commandant, in the attack on Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞將裴叔業入寇徐州，疆埸之民，頗懷去就，高祖憂之，以芳為散騎常侍、國子祭酒、徐州大中正，行徐州事。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan's general Pei Shuye invaded Xuzhou; the people along the frontier were quite uncertain whether to stay or go, and Emperor Xiaowen worried over this, so he made Fang Cavalier Attendant in Ordinary, Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, and acting administrator of Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Luan's general Pei Shuye invaded Xuzhou, many frontier people wavered over whether to stay or defect. Emperor Xiaowen was worried and appointed Fang Cavalier Attendant in Ordinary, Libationer of the Imperial Academy, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, and acting head of Xuzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 徙兼侍中，從征馬圈。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant and followed the campaign against Maquan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant and accompanied the campaign against Maquan.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩於行宮。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen died at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen died at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 及世宗即位，芳手加兗冕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Fang personally placed the ceremonial robe and crown upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Fang personally placed the ceremonial robe and crown on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖自襲斂暨于啟祖、山陵、練除，始末喪事，皆芳撰定。

translations.literal: For Emperor Xiaowen, from dressing and encoffining through the departure rites, the imperial tomb, and the removal of mourning, the funeral matters from beginning to end were all drafted and fixed by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Xiaowen's funeral, from dressing and encoffining through the departure rites, burial at the imperial tomb, and removal of mourning, Fang drafted and settled every procedure from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧等奉申遺旨，令芳入授世宗經。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Xianyang and others respectfully carried out the final instructions and ordered Fang to enter and teach Emperor Shizong the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang and the others carried out the late emperor's instructions by having Fang enter the palace to teach Emperor Shizong the classics.

sentences.zh: 及南徐州刺史沈陵外叛，徐州大水，遣芳撫慰賑恤之。

translations.literal: When Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, rebelled beyond the borders and Xuzhou suffered a great flood, Fang was sent to comfort, reassure, relieve, and aid the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, rebelled outside the realm and Xuzhou was struck by severe flooding, Fang was sent to comfort the people and provide relief.

sentences.zh: 尋正侍中，祭酒、中正並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally made Palace Attendant, while his posts as Libationer and Rectifier remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was confirmed as Palace Attendant, while his posts as Libationer and Rectifier remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 芳表曰：「夫為國家者，罔不崇儒尊道，學校為先，誠復政有質文，茲範不易，諒由萬端資始，眾務禀法故也。

translations.literal: Fang submitted a memorial saying: "Those who govern a state none fail to honor Confucianism and revere the Way, putting schools first—though indeed governance has substance and ornament, this model does not change, presumably because all beginnings draw on it and myriad affairs take their law from it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted a memorial: "Every state-builder venerates learning and exalts the Way, placing schools foremost. Though the form of government may shift between substance and ornament, this standard endures—because all enterprise begins there and every task takes its rule from it.

sentences.zh: 唐虞已往，典籍無據；

translations.literal: From Tang and Yu onward, the classics offer no [direct] evidence;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Zhou, the classics provide no firm record;

sentences.zh: 隆周以降，任居虎門。

translations.literal: From flourishing Zhou downward, the office dwelt at Tiger Gate.
translations.idiomatic: From the height of Zhou times on, the post was lodged at Tiger Gate.

sentences.zh: 周禮大司樂云：[6]『師氏，掌以㜫詔王。

translations.literal: The Director of Music in the Rites of Zhou says: [6] "The Teacher, charged to admonish the king with remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Director of Music, states: [6] "The Master, who admonishes the king with counsels of correction.

sentences.zh: 居虎門之左，司王朝，掌國中失之事，[7]以教國子弟。』

translations.literal: Dwelling to the left of Tiger Gate, overseeing the king's court, administering failures within the state, [7] to teach the sons of the state."
translations.idiomatic: He resided to the left of Tiger Gate, attended the royal court, handled lapses within the realm, [7] and instructed the sons of the nobility."

sentences.zh: 蔡氏勸學篇云：『周之師氏，居虎門左，敷陳六藝，以教國子。』

translations.literal: Cai's Exhortation to Learning says: "Zhou's Teacher dwelt at the left of Tiger Gate, unfolded the Six Arts, to teach the sons of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's Exhortation to Learning reads: "The Zhou Master lived at the left of Tiger Gate, expounded the Six Arts, and trained the royal scions."

sentences.zh: 今之祭酒，即周師氏。

translations.literal: The present Libationer is precisely Zhou's Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Libationer corresponds to the Zhou Master.

sentences.zh: 洛陽記：國子學官與天子宮對，太學在開陽門外。

translations.literal: Records of Luoyang: the National University official [building] faced the Son of Heaven's palace; the Imperial Academy was outside Kaiyang Gate.
