translations.idiomatic: The Records of Luoyang note that the National University's halls faced the imperial palace, while the Imperial Academy stood outside Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 案學記云：『古之王者，建國親民，教學為先。』

translations.literal: Examining the Record of Learning, it says: "The kings of old, establishing the state and drawing the people close, put teaching first."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Learning declares: "Ancient kings, in founding states and cherishing their people, made instruction their first concern."

sentences.zh: 鄭氏注云：『內則設師保以教，使國子學焉，外則有太學、庠序之官。』

translations.literal: Master Zheng's commentary says: "Within, tutors and guardians were appointed to teach, causing the sons of the state to study there; without were the Imperial Academy and orderly schools."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: "Within the palace tutors and guardians taught the royal sons; without stood the Imperial Academy and the school officials."

sentences.zh: 由斯而言，國學在內，太學在外，明矣。

translations.literal: From this it is spoken—the National School is within, the Imperial Academy without—clear.
translations.idiomatic: It follows plainly that the National School lay within and the Imperial Academy without.

sentences.zh: 案如洛陽記，猶有仿像。

translations.literal: Examining as in the Records of Luoyang, there is still a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: If one checks against the Records of Luoyang, the pattern still holds.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂：今既徙縣崧瀍，皇居伊洛，宮闕府寺，僉復故趾，至於國學，豈可舛替？

translations.literal: Your humble servant foolishly holds: now that the capital has moved to Song-Chan, the imperial residence is at Yi-Luo, palaces and government offices all restore former sites—as to the National School, how could it be altered?
translations.idiomatic: I submit: now that the court has moved to the Song-Chan region and the throne sits at Luoyang, palaces and ministries alike have been restored to their former grounds—surely the National School should not be excepted?

sentences.zh: 校量舊事，應在宮門之左。

translations.literal: Comparing with old precedent, it should be at the left of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against ancient practice, it ought to stand to the left of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 至如太學，基所炳在，仍舊營構。

translations.literal: As for the Imperial Academy, its foundation site is clearly marked—still build as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy should remain where its foundations are plainly visible and be rebuilt in the old form.

sentences.zh: 又去太和二十年，[8]發敕立四門博士，於四門置學。

translations.literal: Again, in the twentieth year of Taihe, [8] an edict was issued establishing Four-Gate Erudites and placing schools at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, in Taihe year 20, [8] an edict established Four-Gate Erudites and opened schools at the four city gates.

sentences.zh: 臣案：自周已上，學惟以二，或尚西，或尚東，或貴在國，或貴在郊。

translations.literal: Your servant examines: from Zhou upward, schools were only two—or honoring the west, or honoring the east, or prizing what was in the capital, or prizing what was in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: I find that before Zhou there were only two schools—some traditions favored the west, others the east; some ranked the capital school higher, others the suburban one.

sentences.zh: 爰暨周室，學蓋有六。

translations.literal: Down to the Zhou house, schools altogether numbered six.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhou times there were six schools in all.

sentences.zh: 師氏居內，太學在國，四小在郊。

translations.literal: The Teacher dwelt within; the Imperial Academy was in the capital; the four small [schools] were in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The Master lived inside the palace; the Imperial Academy stood in the capital; the four lesser schools lay in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 禮記云周人『養庶老於虞庠，虞庠在國之四郊』，[9]禮又云：『天子設四學，當入學而太子齒。』

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says the Zhou people "nourished common elders at the Yu school; the Yu school was in the four suburbs of the capital," [9] and the Rites also say: "The Son of Heaven established four schools; when entering school the Crown Prince took rank [by age]."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites states that the Zhou "cared for common elders at the Yu school, situated in the four suburbs," [9] and again: "The Son of Heaven established four schools; when he entered school the crown prince stood among his peers by age."

sentences.zh: 注云：『四學，周四郊之虞庠也。』

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The four schools were the Yu schools in the four suburbs of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss explains: "The four schools were the Yu halls in the Zhou suburbs."

sentences.zh: 案大戴保傅篇云：帝入東學，尚親而貴仁；

translations.literal: Examining the Great Dai's chapter on Tutor and Guardian, it says: the Emperor entered the Eastern School, honoring closeness and esteeming benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: The Great Dai chapter on Tutor and Guardian records: when the emperor entered the Eastern School, he honored kinship and valued benevolence;

sentences.zh: 帝入南學，尚齒而貴信；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Southern School, honoring age and esteeming faithfulness;
translations.idiomatic: entering the Southern School, he honored seniority and valued trustworthiness;

sentences.zh: 帝入西學，尚賢而貴德；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Western School, honoring worth and esteeming virtue;
translations.idiomatic: entering the Western School, he honored talent and valued virtue;

sentences.zh: 帝入北學，尚貴而尊爵；

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Northern School, honoring rank and revering eminence of title;
translations.idiomatic: entering the Northern School, he honored status and revered rank;

sentences.zh: 帝入太學，承師而問道。

translations.literal: the Emperor entered the Imperial Academy, receiving teachers and inquiring about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: entering the Imperial Academy, he received his masters and pursued the Way.

sentences.zh: 周之五學，於此彌彰。

translations.literal: Zhou's five schools are here made all the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's five schools are thus all the more clearly confirmed.

sentences.zh: 案鄭注學記，周則六學。

translations.literal: Examining Master Zheng's commentary on the Record of Learning, in Zhou there were six schools.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Record of Learning holds that Zhou had six schools.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，注云：『內則設師保以教，使國子學焉，外則有太學、庠序之官。』

translations.literal: The reason is this—the commentary says: "Within, tutors and guardians were appointed to teach, causing the sons of the state to study there; without were the Imperial Academy and orderly schools."
translations.idiomatic: The reason, his note runs, is that "within the palace tutors and guardians instructed the royal sons, while without stood the Imperial Academy and the school officials."

sentences.zh: 此其證也。

translations.literal: This is the proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is the evidence.

sentences.zh: 漢魏已降，無復四郊。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei downward, there were no longer four suburbs [schools].
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei times the four suburban schools no longer existed.

sentences.zh: 謹尋先旨，宜在四門。

translations.literal: Respectfully seeking the prior intent, [schools] should be at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Faithful to earlier design, the schools ought to be placed at the four gates.

sentences.zh: 案王肅注云：『天子四郊有學，去王都五十里。』

translations.literal: Examining Wang Su's commentary, it says: "The Son of Heaven had schools in the four suburbs, fifty li from the royal capital."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's note reads: "The Son of Heaven maintained schools in the four suburbs, fifty li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 考之鄭氏，不云遠近。

translations.literal: Examining Master Zheng, he does not speak of distance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, by contrast, says nothing about distance.

sentences.zh: 今太學故坊，基趾寬曠，四郊別置，相去遼闊，檢督難周。

translations.literal: Now the old site of the Imperial Academy has broad foundations; if placed separately in the four suburbs, the distances would be vast and inspection difficult to complete.
translations.idiomatic: The old Imperial Academy grounds are broad enough; scattering schools across four suburbs would spread them impossibly far apart and make oversight impossible.

sentences.zh: 計太學坊并作四門，猶為太廣。

translations.literal: Calculating the Imperial Academy site together with the four gates, it would still be too broad.
translations.idiomatic: Even combining the Imperial Academy grounds with the four gate sites, the area would still be excessive.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚量，同處無嫌。

translations.literal: By your servant's foolish measure, sharing one location gives no offense.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble judgment, housing them together would be unobjectionable.

sentences.zh: 且今時制置，多循中代，未審四學應從古不？

translations.literal: Moreover present institutions mostly follow the middle dynasties—it is not clear whether the four schools should follow antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, current arrangements largely follow middle-period precedent; it is unclear whether the four schools should revert to ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 求集名儒禮官，議其定所。」

translations.literal: Request gathering eminent Confucians and ritual officials to deliberate and fix their locations."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that eminent scholars and ritual officers be convened to determine where they should stand."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The Emperor] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; Libationer as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat while retaining the post of Libationer.

sentences.zh: 出除安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out and was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Qing Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 為政儒緩，不能禁止姦盜，廉清寡欲，無犯公私。

translations.literal: In governance he was Confucian and lenient, unable to suppress wickedness and theft; pure, abstemious, and without violating public or private [interests].
translations.idiomatic: His rule was mild and scholarly; he could not check banditry, yet he was scrupulously honest and free of private greed, offending neither public nor personal trust.

sentences.zh: 還朝，議定律令。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he deliberated on fixing law and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he helped draft the legal code.

sentences.zh: 芳斟酌古今，為大議之主，其中損益，多芳意也。

translations.literal: Fang weighed antiquity and the present, serving as chief of the great deliberation; the additions and subtractions therein were mostly Fang's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang weighed past and present practice and led the major deliberations; most of the revisions bore his mark.

sentences.zh: 世宗以朝儀多闕，其一切諸議，悉委芳修正。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because court ceremony had many omissions, entrusted to Fang the correction of all related deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Because court ritual had many gaps, Emperor Shizong assigned Fang to rectify every outstanding question of ceremony.

sentences.zh: 於是朝廷吉凶大事皆就諮訪焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon on auspicious and inauspicious great affairs of the court, all came to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the court consulted him on every major rite, joyous or mournful.

sentences.zh: 轉太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 芳以所置五郊及日月之位，去城里數於禮有違，又靈星、周公之祀，不應隸太常，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Fang, because the locations set for the five suburban sacrifices and the sun and moon, the distances from the city walls contrary to ritual, and again because the sacrifices to the Spirit Star and Duke of Zhou ought not fall under the Minister of Ceremonies, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fang found that the distances fixed for the five suburban altars and the sites of the sun and moon sacrifices violated ritual propriety, and that worship of the Spirit Star and the Duke of Zhou should not fall under the Minister of Ceremonies. He submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國之大事，莫先郊祀，郊祀之本，實在審位。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that of a state's great affairs, none comes before suburban sacrifice; the root of suburban sacrifice lies truly in determining positions.
translations.idiomatic: I have learned that among a state's weightiest obligations, none precedes suburban sacrifice—and the foundation of suburban sacrifice lies in fixing the altars aright.

sentences.zh: 是以列聖格言，彪炳綿籍；

translations.literal: Hence successive sages' fine words shine brilliantly across extended records;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the luminous admonitions of successive sages blaze across the canon;

sentences.zh: 先儒正論，昭著經史。

translations.literal: former scholars' correct discussions are clearly displayed in classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: and the authoritative commentaries of earlier masters stand forth in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 臣學謝全經，業乖通古，豈可輕薦瞽言，妄陳管說。

translations.literal: Your servant's learning falls short of the whole classics, my craft falls short of penetrating antiquity—how could I lightly recommend a blind man's words or rashly present a narrow view?
translations.idiomatic: My learning is incomplete and my grasp of antiquity uncertain; I dare not offer blind counsel or parade shallow opinions.

sentences.zh: 竊見所置壇祠遠近之宜，考之典制，或未允衷，既曰職司，請陳膚淺。

translations.literal: I have privately seen that the suitability of distances for the established altars and shrines, examined against canonical institutions, may not hit the center; since this is my office, I beg to state what is shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I observe that the distances set for the altars may not accord with canonical practice. As this falls within my charge, I venture a modest proposal.

sentences.zh: 孟春令云「其數八」，又云「迎春於東郊」。

translations.literal: The order for the first month of spring says "its number is eight," and again says "welcome spring at the eastern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The first-spring ordinance states "the number is eight" and also "receive spring at the eastern suburb."

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「東郊，八里之郊也。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says: "The eastern suburb is the suburb of eight li."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi states: "The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburb."

sentences.zh: 賈逵云：「東郊，木帝太昊，八里。」

translations.literal: Jia Kui says: "The eastern suburb—the Wood Emperor Taihao—eight li."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui holds: "The eastern suburb belongs to the Wood Emperor Taihao, eight li away."

sentences.zh: 許慎云：「東郊，八里郊也。」

translations.literal: Xu Shen says: "The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen writes: "The eastern suburb is the eight-li suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄孟春令注云：「王居明堂。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the first-spring order says: "The king dwells in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's gloss on the first-spring ordinance reads: "The king resides in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 禮曰：王出十五里迎歲，蓋殷禮也。

translations.literal: The Rites say: the king goes out fifteen li to welcome the year—presumably Yin rites.
translations.idiomatic: The rites state that the king went out fifteen li to greet the new year—likely Shang practice.

sentences.zh: 周禮，近郊五十里。」

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou: the near suburb is fifty li."
translations.idiomatic: Under the Rites of Zhou, the near suburb lay fifty li away."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄別注云：「東郊，去都城八里。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's separate commentary says: "The eastern suburb is eight li from the capital."
translations.idiomatic: In another note Zheng Xuan specifies: "The eastern suburb stands eight li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 高誘云：「迎春氣於東方，八里郊也。」

translations.literal: Gao You says: "Welcoming the qi of spring in the east—the eight-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Gao You explains: "To receive the breath of spring in the east is the eight-li suburban rite."

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「東郊，八里，因木數也。」

translations.literal: Wang Su says: "The eastern suburb, eight li—following the number of Wood."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su argues: "The eastern suburb is eight li, in accord with the number of Wood."

sentences.zh: 此皆同謂春郊八里之明據也。

translations.literal: These all alike call it clear evidence that the spring suburb is eight li.
translations.idiomatic: All agree: clear proof that the spring suburban altar lies eight li away.

sentences.zh: 孟夏令云「其數七」，又云「迎夏於南郊」。

translations.literal: The order for the first month of summer says "its number is seven," and again says "welcome summer at the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The first-summer ordinance states "the number is seven" and "receive summer at the southern suburb."

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「南郊，七里郊也。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says: "The southern suburb is the seven-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi: "The southern suburb is the seven-li suburb."

sentences.zh: 賈逵云：「南郊，火帝炎帝，七里。」

translations.literal: Jia Kui says: "The southern suburb—the Fire Emperor Yandi—seven li."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui: "The southern suburb belongs to the Fire Emperor Yandi, seven li."

sentences.zh: 許慎云：「南郊，七里郊也。」

translations.literal: Xu Shen says: "The southern suburb is the seven-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen: "The southern suburb is the seven-li suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「南郊，去都城七里。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "The southern suburb is seven li from the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "The southern suburb lies seven li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 高誘云：「南郊，七里之郊也。」

translations.literal: Gao You says: "The southern suburb is the suburb of seven li."
translations.idiomatic: Gao You: "The southern suburb is the seven-li suburban rite."

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「南郊，七里，因火數也。」

translations.literal: Wang Su says: "The southern suburb, seven li—following the number of Fire."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su: "The southern suburb is seven li, in accord with the number of Fire."

sentences.zh: 此又南郊七里之審據也。

translations.literal: This is again solid evidence for the southern suburb at seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Here again is firm proof for the seven-li southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 中央令云：「其數五。」

translations.literal: The central order says: "Its number is five."
translations.idiomatic: The central ordinance states: "The number is five."

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「中郊，五里之郊也。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says: "The central suburb is the suburb of five li."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi: "The central suburb is the five-li suburb."

sentences.zh: 賈逵云；

translations.literal: Jia Kui says;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui writes;

sentences.zh: 「中兆，黃帝之位，并南郊之季，故云兆五帝於四郊也。」

translations.literal: "The central zhao—the position of the Yellow Emperor, combined with the last month of the southern suburb—hence it says 'inaugurate the Five Emperors at the four suburbs.'"
translations.idiomatic: "The central altar is the seat of the Yellow Emperor, combined with the end of the southern suburban season; hence the text speaks of inaugurating the Five Emperors at the four suburbs."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「中郊，西南未地，去都城五里。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "The central suburb—in the Wei corner of the southwest, five li from the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "The central suburb is in the southwest Wei sector, five li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 此又中郊五里之審據也。

translations.literal: This is again solid evidence for the central suburb at five li.
translations.idiomatic: Again, firm proof for the five-li central suburb.

sentences.zh: 孟秋令云「其數九」，又曰：「迎秋於西郊」。

translations.literal: The order for the first month of autumn says "its number is nine," and again: "welcome autumn at the western suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The first-autumn ordinance states "the number is nine" and "receive autumn at the western suburb."

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「西郊，九里郊。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says: "The western suburb is the nine-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi: "The western suburb is the nine-li suburb."

sentences.zh: 賈逵云：「西郊，金帝少皡，九里。」

translations.literal: Jia Kui says: "The western suburb—the Metal Emperor Shaohao—nine li."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui: "The western suburb belongs to the Metal Emperor Shaohao, nine li."

sentences.zh: 許慎云：「西郊，九里郊也。」

translations.literal: Xu Shen says: "The western suburb is the nine-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen: "The western suburb is the nine-li suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「西郊，去都城九里。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "The western suburb is nine li from the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "The western suburb lies nine li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 高誘云：「西郊，九里之郊也。」

translations.literal: Gao You says: "The western suburb is the suburb of nine li."
translations.idiomatic: Gao You: "The western suburb is the nine-li suburban rite."

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「西郊，九里，因金數也。」

translations.literal: Wang Su says: "The western suburb, nine li—following the number of Metal."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su: "The western suburb is nine li, in accord with the number of Metal."

sentences.zh: 此又西郊九里之審據也。

translations.literal: This is again solid evidence for the western suburb at nine li.
translations.idiomatic: Again, firm proof for the nine-li western suburb.

sentences.zh: 孟冬令云「其數六」，又云「迎冬於北郊」。

translations.literal: The order for the first month of winter says "its number is six," and again says "welcome winter at the northern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: The first-winter ordinance states "the number is six" and "receive winter at the northern suburb."

sentences.zh: 盧植云：「北郊，六里郊也。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi says: "The northern suburb is the six-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi: "The northern suburb is the six-li suburb."

sentences.zh: 賈逵云：「北郊，水帝顓頊，六里。」

translations.literal: Jia Kui says: "The northern suburb—the Water Emperor Zhuanxu—six li."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui: "The northern suburb belongs to the Water Emperor Zhuanxu, six li."

sentences.zh: 許慎云：「北郊，六里郊也。」

translations.literal: Xu Shen says: "The northern suburb is the six-li suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen: "The northern suburb is the six-li suburban altar."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「北郊，去都城六里。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "The northern suburb is six li from the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan: "The northern suburb lies six li from the capital."

sentences.zh: 高誘云：「北郊，六里之郊也。」

translations.literal: Gao You says: "The northern suburb is the suburb of six li."
translations.idiomatic: Gao You: "The northern suburb is the six-li suburban rite."

sentences.zh: 王肅云：「北郊六里，因水數也。」

translations.literal: Wang Su says: "The northern suburb, six li—following the number of Water."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su: "The northern suburb is six li, in accord with the number of Water."

sentences.zh: 此又北郊六里之審據也。

translations.literal: This is again solid evidence for the northern suburb at six li.
translations.idiomatic: Again, firm proof for the six-li northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 宋氏含文嘉注云：「周禮，王畿千里，二十分其一以為近郊。

translations.literal: Song's Huwenjia commentary says: "In the Rites of Zhou, the royal domain is a thousand li; one twentieth of it is taken as the near suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Song's commentary on Huwenjia states: "The Rites of Zhou define the royal domain as a thousand li, with one twentieth set aside as the near suburb.

sentences.zh: 近郊五十里，倍之為遠郊。

translations.literal: The near suburb is fifty li; doubling it makes the far suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The near suburb extends fifty li; doubled, it becomes the far suburb.

sentences.zh: 迎王氣蓋於近郊。

translations.literal: Welcoming the king's qi is perhaps at the near suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The reception of the royal qi is presumably conducted at the near suburb.

sentences.zh: 漢不設王畿，則以其方數為郊處，故東郊八里，南郊七里，西郊九里，北郊六里，中郊在西南未地，五里。」

translations.literal: Han did not establish a royal domain, so it took the directional numbers as the suburban sites; hence the eastern suburb eight li, southern seven li, western nine li, northern six li, and the central suburb in the Wei corner of the southwest, five li."
translations.idiomatic: Since Han had no royal domain, it placed the suburban altars according to the directional numbers: eight li east, seven south, nine west, six north, and the central altar in the southwest Wei sector at five li."

sentences.zh: 祭祀志云：「建武二年正月，初制郊兆於雒陽城南七里。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Sacrifices says: "In the first month of the second year of Jianwu, suburban shrines were first established at seven li south of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Sacrifices records: "In the first month of Jianwu 2, suburban altars were first set up seven li south of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 依採元始中故事，北郊在雒陽城北四里。」

translations.literal: Following precedent from the Yuanshi era, the northern suburb was four li north of Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: Following Yuan-shi-era precedent, the northern suburb lay four li north of Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 此又漢世南北郊之明據也。

translations.literal: This is again clear evidence for the northern and southern suburbs in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Here again is explicit proof for Han practice at the northern and southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 今地祇準此。

translations.literal: The altar to Earth is now to follow this standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth altar should now follow this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 至如三十里之郊，進乖鄭玄所引殷周二代之據，退違漢魏所行故事。

translations.literal: As for a thirty-li suburb, taken forward it departs from the evidence Zheng Xuan cites for Yin and Zhou; taken backward it violates Han and Wei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: A thirty-li suburb would run counter both to the Yin and Zhou evidence Zheng Xuan cites and to the precedents followed under Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 凡邑外曰郊，今計四郊，各以郭門為限，里數依上。

translations.literal: Generally, outside the city is called suburb; now calculating the four suburbs, each takes the outer gate as the limit, with the li-count as above.
translations.idiomatic: Land beyond the city walls constitutes the suburbs; the four suburban altars should each be measured from the outer gate, using the distances given above.

sentences.zh: 禮，朝拜日月，皆於東西門外。

translations.literal: By rite, morning worship of the sun and moon takes place outside the eastern and western gates.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual requires worship of the sun and moon outside the eastern and western gates.

sentences.zh: 今日月之位，去城東西路各三十，竊又未審。

translations.literal: Now the positions of the sun and moon are thirty each from the city's east and west roads—I privately am again uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed sites for the sun and moon altars stand thirty paces from the east and west roads, which I still find questionable.

sentences.zh: 禮又云：「祭日於壇，祭月於坎。」

translations.literal: The Rites again say: "Sacrifice to the sun on a mound; sacrifice to the moon in a pit."
translations.idiomatic: The rites further stipulate: "The sun is sacrificed upon a mound; the moon in a pit."

sentences.zh: 今計造如上。

translations.literal: The present plan for construction is as above.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed construction follows the arrangement described above.

sentences.zh: 禮儀志云「立高禖祠于城南」，不云里數。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Ritual says "establish the Gaomei shrine south of the city," without stating the number of li.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Ritual records that the Gaomei shrine was "established south of the city," but gives no distance in li.

sentences.zh: 故今仍舊。

translations.literal: Therefore the present arrangement is retained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, the existing site should remain as it is.

sentences.zh: 靈星本非禮事，兆自漢初，專為祈田，恒隸郡縣。

translations.literal: The Spirit Star was originally not a matter of ritual; its shrine dates from the beginning of Han, devoted solely to praying for harvest, and was always subordinate to the commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Worship of the Spirit Star was never part of canonical ritual; the shrine arose at the start of Han solely to pray for good harvests and always fell under local commandery and county administration.

sentences.zh: 郊祀志云：「高祖五年，[10]制詔御史，其令天下立靈星祠，牲用太牢，縣邑令長侍祠。」

translations.literal: The Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice says: "In the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu,[10] an edict was issued to the Imperial Secretary ordering that Spirit Star shrines be established throughout the realm, with a grand victim, and that magistrates and chiefs of counties and districts attend the sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice records: "In Gaozu's fifth year,[10] an edict to the Imperial Secretary ordered Spirit Star shrines established empire-wide, with grand sacrificial victims, and required county and district magistrates to preside."

sentences.zh: [11]晉祠令云：「郡、縣、國祠稷、社、先農，縣又祠靈星。」

translations.literal: [11] The Jin ordinance on shrines says: "Commanderies, counties, and princely states sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and to the First Farmer; counties additionally sacrifice to the Spirit Star."
translations.idiomatic: [11] The Jin regulations on shrines state: "Commanderies, counties, and princely fiefs maintain altars to soil and grain and to the First Farmer; counties also maintain Spirit Star shrines."

sentences.zh: 此靈星在天下諸縣之明據也。

translations.literal: This is clear evidence that the Spirit Star existed in counties throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is explicit proof that Spirit Star shrines belonged in counties across the empire.

sentences.zh: 周公廟所以別在洛陽者，蓋姬旦創成洛邑，故傳世洛陽，崇祠不絕，以彰厥庸。

translations.literal: The reason the shrine to the Duke of Zhou is separately located in Luoyang is that Ji Dan completed the city of Luo; hence through successive generations in Luoyang, honored sacrifice has never ceased, to manifest his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou shrine stands apart in Luoyang because the Duke of Zhou himself built that city; generation after generation the people of Luoyang have kept his cult alive to honor his achievement.

sentences.zh: 夷齊廟者，亦世為洛陽界內神祠。

translations.literal: The shrine to Boyi and Shuqi likewise has always been a spirit shrine within the bounds of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The shrine to Boyi and Shuqi, too, has long been a local cult within Luoyang's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 今並移太常，恐乖其本。

translations.literal: Now transferring them all to the Minister of Ceremonies would, I fear, betray their original character.
translations.idiomatic: Transferring all such shrines to the Minister of Ceremonies would, I fear, violate their original purpose.

sentences.zh: 天下此類甚眾，皆當部郡縣修理，公私於之禱請。

translations.literal: Cases of this kind are extremely numerous throughout the realm; all should be maintained by their respective commanderies and counties, with public and private persons offering prayers there.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases are legion across the empire; each should remain under its local commandery or county, where officials and common people alike may pray.

sentences.zh: 竊惟太常所司郊廟神祇，自有常限，無宜臨時斟酙以意，若遂爾妄營，則不免淫祀。

translations.literal: I reflect that the suburban shrines and spirits under the Minister of Ceremonies have fixed limits of their own; it is not fitting to measure and apportion them at will; if one then recklessly undertakes such works, one cannot avoid illicit sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban altars and deities under the Minister of Ceremonies have prescribed limits; they should not be rearranged on whim. To do so recklessly would invite the charge of improper worship.

sentences.zh: 二祠在太常，在洛陽，於國一也，然貴在審本。

translations.literal: That the two shrines are under the Minister of Ceremonies, in Luoyang, is one for the state; yet what matters is examining their roots.
translations.idiomatic: Placing both shrines under the Minister of Ceremonies in Luoyang may serve the state equally, but what counts is honoring their origins.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸蔽，謬忝今職，考括墳籍，博採羣議，既無異端，謂粗可依據。

translations.literal: Your servant, being mediocre and ignorant, has wrongly received this present office; examining tomb records and broadly gathering collective opinion, finding no divergent views, I say it may roughly be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and unworthy of my present post, I have searched the tomes and canvassed scholarly opinion; finding no dissent, I believe the proposal may serve as a reasonable guide.

sentences.zh: 今玄冬務隙，野罄人閑，遷易郊壇，二三為便。

translations.literal: Now in deep winter, when tasks are slack and the fields empty and people at leisure, to move the suburban altars would be convenient in two or three respects.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter brings a lull in affairs, empty fields, and idle hands—an apt season to relocate the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「所上乃有明據，但先朝置立已久，且可從舊。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "What you submit has clear evidence, but the former court established these sites long ago; for now, follow the old arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your evidence is sound, but these altars were established long ago; for the present, let the old arrangement stand."

sentences.zh: 先是，高祖於代都詔中書監高閭、太常少卿陸琇并公孫崇等十餘人修理金石及八音之器。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the capital in Dai, Emperor Gaozu ordered Director of the Palace Secretariat Gao Lü, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Lu Pei, Gongsun Chong, and more than ten others to restore metal and stone instruments and the eight kinds of musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, while still at the capital in Dai, Emperor Gaozu had ordered Gao Lü, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Lu Pei, Gongsun Chong, and a dozen others to restore bells, chimes, and the full set of eight musical categories.

sentences.zh: 後崇為太樂令，乃上請尚書僕射高肇，更共營理。

translations.literal: Later, when Chong became Director of Imperial Music, he submitted a request to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Zhao to undertake further restoration together.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Chong became Director of Imperial Music, he petitioned Vice Director Gao Zhao to join him in a further overhaul.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔芳共主之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered Fang to take charge jointly with them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong directed Fang to oversee the work alongside them.

sentences.zh: 芳表以禮樂事大，不容輒決，自非博延公卿，廣集儒彥，討論得失，研窮是非，則無以垂之萬葉，為不朽之式。

translations.literal: Fang submitted a memorial that, because rites and music are a great matter, they cannot be decided rashly; unless one broadly extends invitation to dukes and ministers, widely gathers Confucian scholars of excellence, discusses gains and losses, and investigates right and wrong to the full, one cannot hand them down through myriad generations as an immortal model.
translations.idiomatic: Fang argued that rites and music were too weighty to settle hastily: only by convening the highest officials, assembling eminent scholars, debating every point, and settling every dispute could a lasting standard be established for posterity.

sentences.zh: 被報聽許，數旬之間，頻煩三議。

translations.literal: Having received approval, within several tens of days deliberation was urgently convened three times.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request, and within weeks three formal deliberations were held in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 于時，朝士頗以崇專綜既久，不應乖謬，各默然無發論者。

translations.literal: At the time, court gentlemen largely thought that because Chong had long been in comprehensive charge, he ought not to be in error; each remained silent, with none offering argument.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials largely assumed that Chong, having overseen the project for so long, could not be wrong, and no one spoke up to challenge him.

sentences.zh: 芳乃探引經誥，搜括舊文，共相難質，皆有明據，以為盈縮有差，不合典式。

translations.literal: Fang then drew on canonical admonitions, searched and gathered old texts, and together they questioned and tested one another; all had clear evidence, holding that expansions and contractions had discrepancies and did not accord with canonical models.
translations.idiomatic: Fang cited the classics, marshaled ancient texts, and cross-examined Chong point by point, showing with clear evidence that the proportions were inconsistent and failed to match canonical standards.

sentences.zh: 崇雖示相酬答，而不會問意，卒無以自通。

translations.literal: Although Chong showed responses in kind, he did not meet the intent of the questions and ultimately had no way to justify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong offered rebuttals, but never addressed the questions at issue and ultimately could not defend his work.

sentences.zh: 尚書述奏，[12]仍詔委芳別更考制，於是學者彌歸宗焉。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing submitted a report,[12] and an edict still entrusted Fang separately to examine and formulate anew; thereafter scholars increasingly looked to him as their authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing reported to the throne,[12] and the emperor ordered Fang to undertake a separate review and redesign; from then on, scholars increasingly regarded him as the leading authority.

sentences.zh: 芳以社稷無樹，又上疏曰：「依合朔儀注：日有變，以朱絲為繩，以繞係社樹三匝。

translations.literal: Because the altars of soil and grain had no trees, Fang again submitted a memorial saying: "According to the rites for the new moon: when the sun is eclipsed, use a red silk cord and wrap it three times around the tree of the soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: Finding that the altars of soil and grain had no trees, Fang submitted another memorial: "The new-moon ritual prescribes that during a solar eclipse, a red silk cord is to be wound three times around the altar tree.

sentences.zh: 而今無樹。

translations.literal: Yet now there is no tree.
translations.idiomatic: At present, however, there is no tree.

sentences.zh: 又周禮司徒職云：『設其社稷之壝，而樹之田主，各以其社之所宜木。』

translations.literal: Again, the Rites of Zhou, in the duties of the Minister of Education, say: 'Establish the earthen mounds of the altars of soil and grain and plant trees as lords of the fields, each with the tree appropriate to that altar's soil.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also charge the Minister of Education: 'Raise the earthen mounds of the altars of soil and grain and plant upon them the tree suited to each locality's soil.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：『所宜木，謂若松柏栗也。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'The appropriate tree means such as pine, cypress, and chestnut.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses this: 'The appropriate tree refers to species such as pine, cypress, and chestnut.'

sentences.zh: 此其一證也。

translations.literal: This is the first proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my first piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又小司徒封人職云：『掌設王之社壝，為畿封而樹之。』

translations.literal: Again, the duties of the Junior Minister of Education and the Frontier Officer say: 'In charge of establishing the king's altar mound of soil, marking the royal domain's boundary and planting trees.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also assign the Junior Minister of Education and the Frontier Officer: 'to raise the king's altar mound and plant trees along the royal domain's boundary markers.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注云：『不言稷者，王主於社，稷，社之細也。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'It does not mention grain because the king takes soil as primary; grain is the lesser part of the altar of soil.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'Grain is not named because the king's cult centers on the altar of soil; the grain altar is subsidiary.'

sentences.zh: 此其二證也。

translations.literal: This is the second proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my second piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又論語曰：『哀公問社於宰我，宰我對曰：夏后氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗。』

translations.literal: Again, the Analects says: 'Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altar of soil; Zai Wo replied: "The Xia used pine, the Yin used cypress, the Zhou used chestnut."'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects records: 'When Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altar of soil, Zai Wo answered: "The Xia planted pine, the Shang cypress, the Zhou chestnut."'

sentences.zh: 是乃土地之所宜也。

translations.literal: This is what the land of each place finds suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty chose the tree suited to its own soil.

sentences.zh: 此其三證也。

translations.literal: This is the third proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my third piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 又白虎通云：『社稷所以有樹，何也？

translations.literal: Again, the Baihu tong says: 'Why do the altars of soil and grain have trees?'
translations.idiomatic: The Baihu tong asks: 'Why are trees planted at the altars of soil and grain?'

sentences.zh: 尊而識之也，使民望即見敬之，又所以表功也。』

translations.literal: To honor and mark them, so that when the people look upon them they immediately see and revere them; it is also to display merit.'
translations.idiomatic: To honor and distinguish them, so the people may see them at a glance and pay reverence—and also to display merit.'

sentences.zh: 案此正解所以有樹之義，了不論有之與無也。

translations.literal: Examining this, it rightly explains the meaning of having trees and does not at all discuss whether there are trees or not.
translations.idiomatic: This passage explains why trees belong at the altars; it does not debate whether trees exist at all.

sentences.zh: 此其四證也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fourth piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 此云『社稷所以有樹何』，然則，稷亦有樹明矣也。

translations.literal: This says 'why the altars of soil and grain have trees'; thus, the grain altar too clearly has a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Since the text asks 'why the altars of soil and grain have trees,' the grain altar plainly had a tree as well.

sentences.zh: 又五經通義云：『天子太社、王社，諸侯國社、侯社。

translations.literal: Again, the Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics says: 'The Grand Altar of Soil and the King's Altar of Soil for the Son of Heaven, the State Altar of Soil and the Marquis's Altar of Soil for feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Meaning of the Five Classics also asks: 'What of the Grand Altar of Soil and the King's Altar for the Son of Heaven, and the State Altar and Marquis's Altar for feudal lords?'

sentences.zh: 制度奈何？

translations.literal: What is the institution?
translations.idiomatic: What is the prescribed form?

sentences.zh: 曰：社皆有垣無屋，樹其中以木，有木者土，主生萬物，萬物莫善於木，故樹木也。』

translations.literal: It says: All altars of soil have walls and no roof; trees are planted within them with wood; wood belongs to earth, and earth governs the generation of the myriad things; of the myriad things none is better than wood—hence trees are planted.'
translations.idiomatic: The answer: every altar of soil is walled but roofless, and planted with trees because wood belongs to earth, earth begets the myriad things, and of all things none excels wood—hence the planting of trees.'

sentences.zh: 此其五證也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my fifth piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 此最其丁寧備解有樹之意也。

translations.literal: This most exhaustively and fully explains the intent of having trees.
translations.idiomatic: This passage most fully and carefully explains why trees belong at the altars.

sentences.zh: 又五經要義云：『社必樹之以木。

translations.literal: Again, the Essentials of the Five Classics say: 'The altar of soil must be planted with trees.
translations.idiomatic: The Essentials of the Five Classics also states: 'An altar of soil must be planted with trees.

sentences.zh: 周禮司徒職曰：班社而樹之，各以土地所生。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, in the duties of the Minister of Education, say: Distribute the altars of soil and plant trees, each according to what the land produces.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou charge the Minister of Education: 'Assign the altars of soil and plant trees according to what each region's soil produces.'

sentences.zh: 尚書逸篇曰：太社惟松，東社惟柏，南社惟梓，西社惟栗，北社惟槐。』

translations.literal: A lost chapter of the Documents says: The Grand Altar of Soil has only pine; the Eastern Altar of Soil only cypress; the Southern only catalpa; the Western only chestnut; the Northern only locust.'
translations.idiomatic: A lost passage of the Documents reads: 'The Grand Altar of Soil is pine; the Eastern cypress; the Southern catalpa; the Western chestnut; the Northern locust.'

sentences.zh: 此其六證也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my sixth piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 此又太社及四方皆有樹別之明據也。

translations.literal: This is again clear evidence that the Grand Altar of Soil and the four directions each have distinct trees.
translations.idiomatic: Here again is explicit proof that the Grand Altar and the four directional altars each had its own tree.

sentences.zh: 又見諸家禮圖，社稷圖皆畫為樹，唯誡社、誡稷無樹。

translations.literal: Again, in the ritual diagrams of various schools, the diagrams of the altars of soil and grain all depict trees; only the warning altars of soil and grain have no trees.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual diagrams from various schools likewise depict trees at the altars of soil and grain; only the warning altars omit them.

sentences.zh: 此其七證也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh proof.
translations.idiomatic: This is my seventh piece of evidence.

sentences.zh: 雖辨有樹之據，猶未正所植之木。

translations.literal: Although evidence for having trees has been established, the tree to be planted has not yet been settled.
translations.idiomatic: Though the case for planting trees is now clear, the species to plant remains unsettled.

sentences.zh: 案論語稱『夏后氏以松，殷人以柏，周人以栗』，便是世代不同。

translations.literal: Examining the Analects, which says 'the Xia used pine, the Yin cypress, the Zhou chestnut,' this shows that dynasties differed.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects' record that 'the Xia used pine, the Shang cypress, the Zhou chestnut' shows that each dynasty chose differently.

sentences.zh: 而尚書逸篇則云『太社惟松，東社惟柏，南社惟梓，西社惟栗，北社惟槐』，如此，便以一代之中，而五社各異也。

translations.literal: Yet the lost chapter of the Documents says 'the Grand Altar of Soil has only pine, the Eastern only cypress, the Southern only catalpa, the Western only chestnut, the Northern only locust'—thus, within a single generation, the five altars would each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the lost Documents passage assigns pine to the Grand Altar, cypress to the east, catalpa to the south, chestnut to the west, and locust to the north—implying five different trees within a single reign.

sentences.zh: 愚以為宜植以松。

translations.literal: I think pine should be planted.
translations.idiomatic: I believe pine is the appropriate choice.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How do I say this?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 逸書云『太社惟松』，今者植松，不慮失禮。

translations.literal: The lost book says 'the Grand Altar of Soil has only pine'; to plant pine now need not fear violating ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The lost text states 'the Grand Altar of Soil is pine'; planting pine now would not violate ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 惟稷無成證，乃社之細，蓋亦不離松也。」

translations.literal: Only for grain is there no conclusive proof; being the lesser part of the altar of soil, it probably likewise should not depart from pine."
translations.idiomatic: For the grain altar there is no definitive evidence, but as the subsidiary cult it should presumably follow pine as well.

sentences.zh: 世宗從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 芳沉雅方正，概尚甚高，經傳多通，高祖尤器敬之，動相顧訪。

translations.literal: Fang was deep, elegant, upright, and square; his standards were very high; he was broadly versed in the classics and commentaries; Emperor Gaozu especially valued and respected him, and frequently turned to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was grave, refined, and upright, with exacting standards and broad mastery of the classics. Emperor Gaozu held him in especial esteem and often sought his counsel.

sentences.zh: 太子恂之在東宮，高祖欲為納芳女，芳辭以年貌非宜。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun was in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Gaozu wished to marry Fang's daughter to him; Fang declined on grounds that age and appearance were unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun resided in the Eastern Palace, Emperor Gaozu proposed marrying Fang's daughter to him; Fang declined, citing their unsuitable ages and appearances.

sentences.zh: 高祖歎其謙慎，更敕芳舉其宗女，芳乃稱其族子長文之女。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sighed at his modest caution and further ordered Fang to recommend a clanswoman; Fang then named the daughter of Changwen, a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his modesty and directed him to nominate a kinswoman instead; Fang proposed the daughter of his clansman Changwen.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃為恂娉之，與鄭懿女對為左右孺子焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu then betrothed her to Xun, pairing her with the daughter of Zheng Yi as left and right wet nurses.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu betrothed her to Xun, pairing her with Zheng Yi's daughter as the crown prince's two principal consorts.

sentences.zh: 崔光於芳有中表之敬，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Cui Guang bore the respect due between maternal-cousin relations toward Fang and in every matter sought and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, who was related to Fang through their mothers' families, treated him with cousinly deference and consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 芳撰鄭玄所注周官儀禮音、干寶所注周官音、王肅所注尚書音、何休所注公羊音、范寧所注穀梁音、韋昭所注國語音、范曄後漢書音各一卷，辨類三卷，徐州人地錄四十卷，急就篇續注音義證三卷，毛詩箋音義證十卷，禮記義證十卷，周官、儀禮義證各五卷。

translations.literal: Fang compiled one fascicle each of the pronunciations of Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Offices of Zhou and the Ceremonial Rites, Gan Bao's commentary on the Offices of Zhou, Wang Su's commentary on the Documents, He Xiu's commentary on the Gongyang, Fan Ning's commentary on the Guliang, Wei Zhao's commentary on the Discourses of the States, and Fan Ye's pronunciations for the Book of Later Han; three fascicles of classified distinctions; forty fascicles of the Record of the Land and People of Xuzhou; three fascicles continuing the phonetic meanings and evidence of the Rapid Writing Primer; ten fascicles of phonetic meanings and evidence for the Mao Commentary on the Odes; ten fascicles of evidential commentary on the Record of Rites; and five fascicles each of evidential commentary on the Offices of Zhou and the Ceremonial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fang authored one fascicle each on the pronunciation of Zheng Xuan's Zhou Offices and Ceremonial Rites, Gan Bao's Zhou Offices, Wang Su's Documents, He Xiu's Gongyang Commentary, Fan Ning's Guliang Commentary, Wei Zhao's Discourses of the States, and Fan Ye's Book of Later Han; three fascicles of lexical distinctions; forty fascicles on the geography and people of Xuzhou; three fascicles continuing the phonetic glosses and evidence for the Rapid Writing Primer; ten fascicles of phonetic evidence for the Mao Odes; ten fascicles of evidential commentary on the Record of Rites; and five fascicles each on the Zhou Offices and Ceremonial Rites.

sentences.zh: 崔光表求以中書監讓芳，世宗不許。

translations.literal: Cui Guang submitted a memorial requesting to yield the post of Director of the Palace Secretariat to Fang; Emperor Shizong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang petitioned to resign the directorship of the Palace Secretariat in Fang's favor, but Emperor Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yan Chang he died, at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yan Chang 2, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔賜帛四百匹，贈鎮東將軍、徐州刺史，諡文貞。

translations.literal: An edict granted four hundred bolts of silk; he was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted four hundred bolts of silk and posthumously honored him as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous name Wenzhen, "Cultivated and Steadfast."

sentences.zh: 長子懌，字祖欣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yi, styled Zuxin.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Yi, courtesy name Zuxin.

sentences.zh: 雅有父風，頗好文翰。

translations.literal: Elegantly he had his father's manner and was rather fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's refined bearing and had a taste for letters.

sentences.zh: 歷徐州別駕、兗州左軍府長史、司空諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Aide of Xuzhou, Chief Clerk of the Left Army Staff of Yan Province, and Advisory Attendant of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as Aide of Xuzhou, Chief Clerk on the Left Army staff of Yan Province, and Advisory Attendant to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 屢為行臺出使，所歷皆有當官之稱。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he went out as envoy for the Mobile Secretariat; wherever he served he earned the reputation of fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as an envoy for the Mobile Secretariat and earned a reputation for competence wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍、徐州大中正、行郢州事，尋遷安南將軍、大司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, acting Administrator of Ying Province; soon after he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Minister of Grand Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, and acting Administrator of Ying Province, then soon after to General Who Pacifies the South and Minister of Grand Granaries.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東將軍、徐州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou, with the posthumous name Jian, "Concise."

sentences.zh: 無子，弟廞以第三子㻐為後。

translations.literal: Having no son, his younger brother Yin made his third son Bi heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his younger brother Yin adopted his third son Bi as heir.

sentences.zh: 㻐，天平中，走江南。

translations.literal: Bi, in the Tianping era, fled to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fled south to Jiangnan during the Tianping era.

sentences.zh: 武定末，歸國，賜爵臨潁縣子。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era, he returned to the state and was granted the title Viscount of Linying County.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he returned north and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linying County.

sentences.zh: 懌弟廞，字景興。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Yin, styled Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother was Yin, courtesy name Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 好學強立，善事當世。

translations.literal: Fond of learning and strong in self-reliance, he was good at managing affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, stood firmly on his own principles, and handled the affairs of his day with skill.

sentences.zh: 高肇之盛及清河王懌為宰輔，廞皆與其子姪交遊往來。

translations.literal: At the height of Gao Zhao's power and when the Prince of Qinghe, Yi, served as chief minister, Yin associated and exchanged visits with their sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: During Gao Zhao's ascendancy and Prince of Qinghe Yi's tenure as chief minister, Yin cultivated ties with their sons and nephews, visiting back and forth.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，又與太后兄弟往還相好，太后令廞以詩賦授弟元吉。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, he again exchanged visits on friendly terms with the empress dowager's brothers; the empress dowager had Yin instruct her younger brother Yuan Ji in poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Ling took the regency, he also kept up a warm exchange with her brothers; the empress dowager appointed him to teach poetry and fu to her younger brother Yuan Ji.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、太尉屬、中書侍郎，冠軍將軍、行南青州事，尋徵安南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He served successively as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Aide of the Grand Commandant, and Deputy Director of the Palace Secretariat; as General Who Establishes Courage and acting Administrator of Southern Qing Province; soon after he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Aide of the Grand Commandant, and Deputy Director of the Palace Secretariat, then served as General Who Establishes Courage and acting Administrator of Southern Qing Province before being recalled as General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，除國子祭酒，復以本官行徐州事。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was appointed Director of the Imperial University and again served in his existing rank as acting Administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang first took the throne, he was made Director of the Imperial University and continued in that capacity as acting Administrator of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，除驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Under the former Deposed Emperor he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Under the former Deposed Emperor he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，除散騎常侍，遷驃騎大將軍，復領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Chu's reign he was appointed Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and again put in charge of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu first acceded, he was made Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary, then promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry while resuming his post as Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 出帝於顯陽殿講孝經，廞為執經，雖詶答論難未能精盡，而風彩音制足有可觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Xianyang Hall, Yin held the classic text; although his responses and debate did not reach full refinement, his bearing and voice were well worth seeing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu expounded the Classic of Filial Piety in the Xianyang Hall, Yin served as lecturer. His answers in debate were not always exhaustive, yet his presence and delivery were impressive enough to watch.

sentences.zh: 尋兼都官尚書，又兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Soon after he concurrently served as Director of Judgments and also as Director of the Palace Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent appointment as Director of Judgments and then as Director of the Palace Gentlemen as well.

sentences.zh: 及出帝入關，齊獻武王至洛，責廞而誅之，時年五十二。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu entered the Pass, King Xianwu of Qi reached Luoyang, rebuked Yin, and executed him; he was then fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Chu fled west of the Pass, King Xianwu of Qi entered Luoyang, held Yin to account, and had him put to death. He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 子騭，字子昇。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhi, courtesy name Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: In youth he had spirit and bearing and was fairly versed in letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he had force of character and a solid grounding in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州辟主簿，奉使詣闕，見莊帝於顯陽殿，問以邊事。

translations.literal: At twenty the province recruited him as chief clerk; sent on mission to court, he was received by Emperor Zhuang in the Xianyang Hall and questioned about frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recruited by his province as chief clerk. On a mission to court he was received by Emperor Xiaozhuang in the Xianyang Hall and questioned about border affairs.

sentences.zh: 騭應對閑敏，帝善之，遂敕除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhi replied with easy quickness; the emperor approved and thereupon ordered his appointment as Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered with poised ease, and the emperor was pleased; he was thereupon appointed Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 出補徐州開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He left court to fill the post of Attendant of the Eastern Department in the Xuzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Attendant of the Eastern Department on the Xuzhou headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 父廞之死，騭率勒鄉部赴兗州，與刺史樊子鵠抗禦王師，每戰流涕突陳。

translations.literal: At his father Yin's death, Zhi led the local militia to Yan Province, joined Governor Fan Zihe in resisting the royal army, and in every battle wept as he charged the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Yin was executed, Zhi rallied the local militia and marched to Yan Province, where he and Governor Fan Zihe resisted the royal army; in every battle he wept as he broke through the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 城陷，擒送晉陽，齊獻武王矜而赦之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured and sent to Jinyang; King Xianwu of Qi took pity and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell he was captured and sent to Jinyang, where King Xianwu of Qi spared him out of compassion.

sentences.zh: 文襄王之為儀同開府，以騭為屬。

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang held the rank of Commander Unequaled in Honor with a headquarters, he made Zhi an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang opened a headquarters as Commander Unequaled in Honor, he took Zhi on as an aide.

sentences.zh: 本州大中正。

translations.literal: Grand Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 武定初，轉中書舍人，加安東將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of the Wuding era he was transferred to Palace Secretariat Attendant and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 於時與蕭衍和通，騭前後受敕接對其使十六人。

translations.literal: At that time, when peace and contact were established with Xiao Yan, Zhi received repeated orders to receive and answer his envoys, sixteen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: While relations with Xiao Yan were open, Zhi was repeatedly ordered to receive Liang envoys; he handled sixteen such missions in all.

sentences.zh: 出為司徒右長史，未幾遷左長史。

translations.literal: He left court as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; before long he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and soon afterward promoted to Left Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 六年，受使兗州，行達東郡，暴疾卒，時人嗟惜之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, while on mission to Yan Province and traveling as far as Dong Commandery, he died suddenly of illness; men of the time lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on a mission to Yan Province, he fell suddenly ill and died at Dong Commandery; contemporaries mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 追贈本將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed with his former general's rank and as Governor of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with his former general's rank and the governorship of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 廞弟悅，永安中，開府記室。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Yue, in the Yong'an era, served as Recorder of a headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Yue served as headquarters recorder during the Yong'an era.

sentences.zh: 悅弟戫，武定中，鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yue's younger brother Hou, in the Wuding era, held the ranks of General Who Guards the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's younger brother Hou held the ranks of General Who Guards the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 戫弟粹，徐州別駕、朱衣直閤。

translations.literal: Hou's younger brother Cui served as Aide of Xuzhou and Attendant in Scarlet Robes of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Hou's younger brother Cui held the posts of Aide of Xuzhou and Attendant in Scarlet Robes of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 粹少尚氣俠，兄廞死，粹招合部曲，就兗州刺史樊子鵠，謀應關西。

translations.literal: Cui in youth prized chivalric spirit; when his elder brother Yin died, Cui gathered retainers, went to Yan Province Governor Fan Zihe, and plotted to respond to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui had a chivalrous temperament from youth. After his brother Yin was killed, he rallied a private following, joined Yan Province Governor Fan Zihe, and plotted to side with the regime west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 大將軍攻討，城陷，殺之。

translations.literal: The Grand General attacked and suppressed him;[13] when the city fell, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A grand general besieged and crushed the revolt;[13] when the city fell, Cui was put to death.

sentences.zh: 芳叔撫之，孫思祖，勇健有將略。

translations.literal: Fang's paternal uncle was Fuzhi. Sun Simo was brave and fit, with talent for command.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's paternal uncle was Fuzhi. Sun Simo was bold and vigorous, with real skill as a commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖末入朝，歷羽林監，梁、沛二郡太守，員外常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Gaozu's reign he entered court service, serving successively as Colonel of the Feathered Forest Guard, Administrator of the two commanderies of Liang and Pei, and Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Gaozu's reign he entered court service, rising through the posts of Colonel of the Feathered Forest Guard, Administrator of Liang and Pei commanderies, and Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 屢為統軍南征，累著功捷。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he served as army commander on southern campaigns and accumulated distinguished achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly commanded armies on southern campaigns and won a string of victories.

sentences.zh: 任城王之圍鍾離也，蕭衍遣其冠軍將軍張惠紹及彭瓫、張豹子等率眾一萬送糧鍾離。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Rencheng besieged Zhongli, Xiao Yan sent his General Who Establishes Courage Zhang Huishao, together with Peng Fu, Zhang Baozi, and others, leading ten thousand men to deliver grain to Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince of Rencheng was besieging Zhongli, Xiao Yan dispatched his General Who Establishes Courage Zhang Huishao, along with Peng Fu, Zhang Baozi, and others, with ten thousand men to convoy supplies to the city.

sentences.zh: 時思祖為平遠將軍，領兵數千邀衍餉軍於邵陽，遣其長史元龜步騎一千，[14]於鍾離之北遏其前鋒，錄事參軍繆琰掩其後，思祖身率精銳橫衝其陳，三軍合擊，大破之，擒惠紹及衍驍騎將軍、祁陽縣開國男趙景悅、悅弟寧遠將軍景脩、寧遠將軍梅世和、屯騎校尉任景攸、長水校尉邊欣、越騎校尉賈慶真、龍驤將軍徐敞等，俘斬數千人。

translations.literal: At the time Simo was General Who Pacifies the Distant, leading several thousand men to intercept Xiao Yan's supply army at Shaoyang; he sent his Chief Clerk Yuan Gui with a thousand infantry and cavalry[14] to block the vanguard north of Zhongli, had Recording Secretary Miao Yan strike from the rear, and himself led picked troops in a cross charge against their formation; the three forces combined in attack and routed them utterly, capturing Huishao and Xiao Yan's General of Agile Cavalry, Baron of Qiyang County Zhao Jingyue, Jingyue's younger brother General Who Pacifies the Distant Jing Xiu, General Who Pacifies the Distant Mei Shihe, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Ren Jingyou, Colonel of the Regular Cavalry Bian Xin, Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry Jia Qingzhen, General of the Flying Dragon Xu Chang, and others, taking or slaying several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Simo, then General Who Pacifies the Distant, led several thousand men to intercept the Liang supply train at Shaoyang. He sent his chief clerk Yuan Gui with a thousand infantry and cavalry[14] to block the enemy vanguard north of Zhongli, had his recording secretary Miao Yan fall on their rear, and personally led elite troops in a flanking charge. The three wings struck together and won a crushing victory, capturing Huishao along with Xiao Yan's General of Agile Cavalry, Baron of Qiyang County Zhao Jingyue, Jingyue's younger brother General Who Pacifies the Distant Jing Xiu, General Who Pacifies the Distant Mei Shihe, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry Ren Jingyou, Colonel of the Regular Cavalry Bian Xin, Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry Jia Qingzhen, General of the Flying Dragon Xu Chang, and others, while killing or capturing several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 尚書論功擬封千戶侯。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing debated his merit and proposed enfeoffing him as Marquis with a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing reviewed his merit and proposed enfeoffing him as a marquis with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 思祖有二婢，美姿容，善歌舞，侍中元暉求之不得，事遂停寢。

translations.literal: Simo had two maidservants of beautiful appearance who were skilled in song and dance; Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui sought them but did not obtain them, and the matter was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: Simo had two maidservants of striking beauty who sang and danced well. Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui demanded them and was refused, and the enfeoffment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 後除揚烈將軍、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Raises Might and Administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Raises Might and Administrator of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 思祖於路叛奔蕭衍，衍以思祖為輔國將軍、北徐州刺史，頻寇淮北。

translations.literal: Simo defected on the road and fled to Xiao Yan; Yan made Simo General Who Supports the State and Governor of Northern Xuzhou, and he repeatedly raided north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Simo defected en route to Xiao Yan, who made him General Who Supports the State and Governor of Northern Xuzhou; he then raided the Huai River north country repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 數年而死。

translations.literal: After several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 纘子晰，歷蕭衍琅邪、東莞二郡太守，戍朐山。

translations.literal: Zuan's son Xi served successively as Administrator of the two commanderies of Langye and Dongguan under Xiao Yan and garrisoned Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's son Xi served under Xiao Yan as Administrator of Langye and Dongguan commanderies in turn and held the garrison at Qushan.

sentences.zh: 朐山人王萬壽斬晰，送首，以朐山內附，并晰子翐於京師。

translations.literal: Wang Wanshou of Qushan beheaded Xi and sent the head; he submitted Qushan to allegiance and also sent Xi's son Chi to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wanshou of Qushan killed Xi and sent his head, bringing Qushan over to Wei allegiance and sending Xi's son Chi to the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 數年後，以翐為給事中、汝陽太守。

translations.literal: Several years later Chi was appointed Supervisor within the Gates and Administrator of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later Chi was made Supervisor within the Gates and Administrator of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 正光初，自郡南叛。

translations.literal: At the start of the Zhengguang era he defected south from his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengguang he defected south from his post.

sentences.zh: 芳從子懋，字仲華。

translations.literal: Fang's paternal cousin's son Mao, styled Zhonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's paternal cousin's son was Mao, courtesy name Zhonghua.

sentences.zh: 祖泰之，父承伯，仕於劉彧，並有名位。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Taizhi; his father was Chengbo; both served Liu Yu and held noted rank and position.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Taizhi and his father Chengbo had both served Liu Yu and attained distinguished rank.

sentences.zh: 懋聰敏好學，博綜經史，善草隸書，多識奇字。

translations.literal: Mao was clever and fond of learning, broadly versed in the classics and histories, skilled in cursive and clerical script, and knew many unusual characters.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was bright and studious, with wide command of the classics and histories, a practiced hand in cursive and clerical script, and an unusual store of rare characters.

sentences.zh: 世宗初入朝，拜員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong first entered court service, Mao was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong first came to court, Mao was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書外兵郎中，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of External Military Affairs in the Masters of Writing and given the additional title General of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman of External Military Affairs in the Masters of Writing and given the additional rank of General of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 芳甚重之，凡所撰制朝廷軌儀，皆與參量。

translations.literal: Fang greatly valued him; in all regulations and court ritual that were drafted, Mao joined in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Fang held him in high regard and consulted him on every draft of court ritual and regulation.

sentences.zh: 尚書博議，懋與殿中郎袁翻常為議主。

translations.literal: At broad deliberations of the Masters of Writing, Mao and Palace Attendant Yuan Fan often served as chief debaters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Masters of Writing's full deliberations, Mao and Palace Attendant Yuan Fan were regularly the leading voices.

sentences.zh: 達於從政，臺中疑事，咸所訪決。

translations.literal: Skilled in administration, he was consulted and decided on all doubtful matters within the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Adept at practical governance, he was the man the secretariat turned to whenever a case was unclear.

sentences.zh: 受詔參議新令。

translations.literal: He received an edict to join deliberation on the new ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he took part in drafting the new legal code.

sentences.zh: 性沉雅厚重，善與人交，器宇淵曠，風流甚美，時論高之。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep, refined, and weighty; skilled in friendship; his bearing was broad and far-reaching; his elegance was very fine; opinion of the time held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature grave, refined, and steady, easy in friendship, with a breadth of bearing and an elegance that contemporaries greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 尚書李平，與之結莫逆之友。

translations.literal: Minister Li Ping formed with him a friendship of utmost trust.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Ping became his closest friend.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，領郎中，兼東宮中舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, put in charge of Gentlemen, and concurrently served as Attendant of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Colonel of the Footsoldiers, placed in charge of the Gentlemen, and given concurrent appointment as Attendant of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 轉員外常侍、鎮遠將軍，領考功郎中，立考課之科，明黜陟之法，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Distant, put in charge of the Gentleman of Merit Assessment, established categories for merit review, clarified methods of promotion and demotion, and was very systematic.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Distant, placed in charge of merit assessment, and drew up a clear system of evaluation with explicit rules for promotion and demotion.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，大軍攻硤石，懋為李平行臺郎中，城拔，懋頗有功。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign the great army attacked Xiashi; Mao served as Gentleman of Li Ping's Mobile Secretariat; when the city was taken, Mao had considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong first took the throne, the main army besieged Xiashi. Mao served on Li Ping's mobile staff and distinguished himself when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌愛其風雅，常目而送之曰：「劉生堂堂，搢紳領袖，若天假之年，必為魏朝宰輔。」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, loved his refinement; he often watched him depart and said: "Master Liu is imposing—the leader among court gentlemen; if Heaven grants him years, he will surely become chief minister of the Wei court."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, admired his literary grace and would often watch him leave, saying, "Master Liu is a commanding presence—the foremost man among the court elite. If Heaven grants him a full span of years, he will surely become chief minister of Wei."

sentences.zh: 詔懋與諸才學之士，撰成儀令。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Mao, together with other men of talent and learning, to compile completed ritual ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Mao and other learned officials to compile the completed ritual code.

sentences.zh: 懌為宰相積年，禮懋尤重，令諸子師之。

translations.literal: Yi served as chief minister for many years and treated Mao with especial honor, ordering his sons to take Mao as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had been chief minister for years and treated Mao with exceptional respect, appointing him tutor to his sons.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Administrator of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年冬，暴病卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiping he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Xiping 2 he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 家甚清貧，亡之日，徒四壁而已。

translations.literal: His household was very poor and clean; on the day of his death there were only bare walls.
translations.idiomatic: His household was deeply poor; when he died he left nothing but bare walls.

sentences.zh: 太傅懌及當時才儁莫不痛惜之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Yi and the outstanding men of the time all grieved and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yi and the leading men of the age all mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈持節、前將軍、南秦州刺史，諡曰宣簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed with the Ceremonial Axe, as Former General and Governor of Southern Qin Province; posthumous title Xuansjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the Ceremonial Axe as Former General and Governor of Southern Qin Province, with the posthumous name Xuansjian, "Proclaiming Concision."

sentences.zh: 懋詩誄賦頌及諸文筆，見稱於時，又撰諸器物造作之始十五卷，名曰物祖。

translations.literal: Mao's poems, dirges, rhapsodies, eulogies, and various writings were praised in his time; he also compiled fifteen scrolls on the origins of the making of various implements, entitled Origins of Things.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's poetry, dirges, rhapsodies, eulogies, and other writings won praise in his day. He also compiled fifteen scrolls on the origins of various artifacts, entitled Origins of Things.

sentences.zh: 子筠，字士貞。

translations.literal: His son Jun, styled Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jun, courtesy name Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 自員外散騎侍郎，歷河南郡丞、中散大夫、徐州大中正、祕書丞。

translations.literal: From Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier he served successively as Assistant Administrator of Henan Commandery, Palace Attendant, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, and Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Starting from Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier, he rose through the posts of Assistant Administrator of Henan Commandery, Palace Attendant, Grand Rectifier of Xuzhou, and Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 天平初卒。

translations.literal: At the start of the Tianping era he died.
