translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Tianping era.

sentences.zh: 贈前將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Former General and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Former General and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子規，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Gui died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui died young.

sentences.zh: 筠弟筟，字士文。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Fu, styled Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother was Fu, courtesy name Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 少而聰惠。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 年十二，詣尚書王衍，衍與語大奇之，遂與太傅李延寔、祕書李凱上疏薦之，拜祕書郎。

translations.literal: At age twelve he went to see Minister Wang Yan; Yan spoke with him and was greatly struck; thereupon, together with Grand Tutor Li Yanshi and Palace Librarian Li Kai, he submitted a memorial recommending him, and Fu was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he visited Minister Wang Yan, who was astonished by their conversation. Yan then joined Grand Tutor Li Yanshi and Palace Librarian Li Kai in recommending him by memorial, and Fu was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 筟亦善士。

translations.literal: Fu was also a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was also a man of fine character.

sentences.zh: 興和元年卒，年二十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xinghe he died, at age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xinghe 1, at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 無子，兄子矩繼。

translations.literal: Having no son, his elder brother's son Ju succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his elder brother's son Ju became his heir.

sentences.zh: 懋從叔元孫，養志丘園，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Mao's paternal cousin Yuansun nourished his aspirations in hill and garden and did not seek fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's paternal cousin Yuansun cultivated his life in retirement and sought neither fame nor office.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸彭城，起家拜蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu visited Pengcheng, Yuansun was first appointed from private life as Administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu visited Pengcheng, Yuansun was summoned from private life and appointed Administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 治以清靜為名。

translations.literal: His governance was famed for clarity and tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was known for its quiet integrity.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子長文，高祖擢為南兗州冠軍府長史，帶譙郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Changwen was selected by Emperor Gaozu as Chief Clerk of the Headquarters of the General Who Establishes Courage in Southern Yan Province, concurrently serving as Administrator of Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changwen was promoted by Emperor Gaozu to Chief Clerk of the Southern Yan headquarters of the General Who Establishes Courage, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Qiao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 被圍糧竭，固節全城，以功賜爵下邑子。

translations.literal: Besieged until grain was exhausted, he held firm and preserved the whole city; for his merit he was granted the title Viscount of a Lesser Settlement.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was besieged and supplies ran out, he held his post and preserved the whole city; for this he was enfeoffed as Viscount of a Lesser Settlement.

sentences.zh: 遷魯郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrator of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖為太子恂納其女為孺子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter in marriage for Crown Prince Xun as a consort of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as consort for Crown Prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子敬先，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jingxian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxian succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 敬先弟徽，奉朝請，徐州治中。

translations.literal: Jingxian's younger brother Hui served as Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance and Chief Administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxian's younger brother Hui served as Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance and Chief Administrator of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 長文弟永，字履南。

translations.literal: Changwen's younger brother Yong, styled Lünan.
translations.idiomatic: Changwen's younger brother was Yong, courtesy name Lünan.

sentences.zh: 頗有將略，累著征戰之勤。

translations.literal: He had considerable talent for command and repeatedly showed merit in campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He had real military talent and won repeated distinction in the field.

sentences.zh: 歷位中散大夫、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Palace Attendant and General of the Flying Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the ranks of Palace Attendant and General of the Flying Dragon.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，兼大鴻臚卿，持策拜高麗王安。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he concurrently served as Minister of Grand Reception, bearing credentials to invest the King of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era he served concurrently as Minister of Grand Reception and went with imperial credentials to invest the King of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 還，除范陽太守。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Administrator of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 芳族兄僧利，輕財通俠，甚得鄉情。

translations.literal: Fang's clansman elder brother Sengli was generous with wealth and open in chivalry, and was greatly trusted by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's clansman Sengli was free with his wealth and well known for chivalrous conduct; he enjoyed deep goodwill in his home district.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸徐州，引見，善之，拜徐州別駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu visited Xuzhou he was summoned for audience; the emperor approved and appointed him Aide of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu visited Xuzhou, Sengli was summoned to audience, pleased the emperor, and was appointed Aide of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷沛郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrator of Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後遂從容鄉里，不樂臺官。

translations.literal: Later he settled at ease in his home district and did not delight in capital office.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired to an easy life at home and had no taste for office at court.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，朝議慮其有二志，徵拜輕車將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, court deliberation feared he had divided loyalties and summoned him, appointing him General of Light Chariots and Colonel of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years away from court, the government feared he might harbor divided loyalties and recalled him as General of Light Chariots and Colonel of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 長子世雄，至太山太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shixiong rose to Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shixiong rose to the governorship of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 世雄弟世明，字伯楚，頗涉書傳。

translations.literal: Shixiong's younger brother Shiming, styled Bochu, was fairly versed in the classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong's younger brother was Shiming, courtesy name Bochu, with a solid grounding in the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請稍遷蘭陵太守、彭城內史。

translations.literal: Starting from Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance, he was gradually promoted to Administrator of Lanling and Interior Minister of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance, he rose in stages to Administrator of Lanling and Interior Minister of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 屬刺史元法僧以城外叛，遂送蕭衍。

translations.literal: Just then the Prefect Yuan Faseng rebelled outside the city and delivered him to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the regional inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled outside the city walls, Shiming was handed over to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍欲加封爵，世明固辭不受，頻請衍乞還，衍聽之。

translations.literal: Yan wished to grant him a title and fief; Shiming firmly declined and would not accept, repeatedly begging Yan to allow his return; Yan granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan wished to ennoble him, but Shiming steadfastly refused; he repeatedly begged to be allowed to return north, and Yan consented.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，徵為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: During Emperor Suzong's reign, he was summoned and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Suzong, he was summoned to court as Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 孝莊末，除征虜將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Prefect of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, he was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Prefect of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 時尒朱世隆等威權自己，四方怨叛，城民王乞得逼劫世明，據州歸蕭衍。

translations.literal: At that time Erzhu Shilong and others wielded power as they pleased; rebellion and resentment spread across the realm. The city resident Wang Qide forcibly coerced Shiming, seized the province, and submitted to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and his faction had seized power for themselves, and discontent and rebellion spread everywhere. A townsman named Wang Qide forced Shiming at sword-point, seized the province, and submitted it to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍封世明開國縣侯，食邑千戶，征西大將軍、郢州刺史，又加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yan enfeoffed Shiming as Marquis of Kaiguo County with a fief of one thousand households, made him Grand General Who Conquers the West and Prefect of Ying Province, and additionally granted him the honors of the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan enfeoffed Shiming as Marquis of Kaiguo County with a fief of one thousand households, appointed him Grand General Who Conquers the West and Prefect of Ying Province, and further granted him the honors of the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 世明復辭不受，固請北歸。

translations.literal: Shiming again declined and would not accept, steadfastly requesting to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Shiming again refused the honors and pressed his request to return to the north.

sentences.zh: 衍不奪其意，乃躬餞之於樂遊苑。

translations.literal: Yan did not oppose his wish and personally saw him off with a farewell feast at Leyou Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan would not override his wishes and personally hosted a farewell banquet for him at Leyou Garden.

sentences.zh: 世明既還，奉送所持節，身歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Once Shiming had returned, he formally surrendered the credentials he had held and went home in person.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, Shiming formally surrendered the imperial credentials he had held and withdrew to his home district.

sentences.zh: 自是不復入朝，常以射獵為適。

translations.literal: From then on he never again entered court, and usually took archery and hunting as his pastime.
translations.idiomatic: He never entered court again thereafter, and passed his days chiefly in archery and hunting.

sentences.zh: 興和三年卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xinghe era he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the honors of the Three Preceptors, and Prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with the honors of the Three Preceptors, and as Prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子禕，字彥英。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Yan'ying.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, courtesy name Yan'ying.

sentences.zh: 武定末，冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, General Who Establishes the Champion and Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he held the ranks of General Who Establishes the Champion and Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 初，蘭陵繆儼靈奇，與彭城劉氏才望略等。

translations.literal: Earlier, Miao Yan Lingqi of Lanling was roughly equal in talent and reputation to the Liu clan of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days Miao Yan Lingqi of Lanling had been roughly equal in talent and standing to the Liu family of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 及彭城內附，靈奇弟子承先隨薛安都至京師，賜爵襄賁子，尋還徐州，數十年間，了無從官者。

translations.literal: When Pengcheng submitted to the north, Lingqi's disciple's son Chengxian followed Xue Andu to the capital, was granted the title Viscount of Xiangben, and soon returned to Xuzhou; for several decades there was scarcely anyone in office from his line.
translations.idiomatic: After Pengcheng submitted to the Wei, Lingqi's disciple's son Chengxian followed Xue Andu to the capital, was granted the title Viscount of Xiangben, and soon returned to Xuzhou; for decades afterward scarcely anyone from that line held office.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，承先子彥植襲爵，見叙，稍遷伏波將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, Chengxian's son Yanzhi inherited the title, was entered in the registers, and was gradually promoted to General Who Quells the Waves and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, Chengxian's son Yanzhi inherited the title, was entered on the rolls of service, and was gradually promoted to General Who Quells the Waves and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 彥植恭慎長厚，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was respectful, cautious, and steadfastly generous, and was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was respectful, cautious, and generous of spirit, and won praise from his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 時滎陽鄭演，仕劉彧為琅邪太守。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Yan of Xingyang served Liu Yu as Administrator of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Yan of Xingyang served Liu Yu as Administrator of Langye.

sentences.zh: 屬徐州刺史薛安都將謀內附，演贊成其事。

translations.literal: When the Prefect of Xuzhou Xue Andu was about to plot submission to the north, Yan supported the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andu, Prefect of Xuzhou, was planning to submit to the north, Yan supported the move.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初入朝，以功除冠軍將軍、彭城太守、洛陽侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu first entered court, he was appointed for his merit General Who Establishes the Champion, Administrator of Pengcheng, and Marquis of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu first came to court, Yan was rewarded for his service with the posts of General Who Establishes the Champion and Administrator of Pengcheng, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後拜太中大夫，改爵雲陽伯。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Consultation and his title was changed to Earl of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Consultation, and his title was changed to Earl of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Prefect of You Province, with posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Prefect of You Province, with the posthumous name Yi, "Benevolent."

sentences.zh: 其子孫因此遂家彭、泗。

translations.literal: His descendants therefore made their home in the Peng and Si regions.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants therefore settled in the Peng and Si region.

sentences.zh: 子長猷，以父勳起家，拜寧遠將軍、東平太守。

translations.literal: His son Changyou, beginning his career through his father's merit, was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyou entered official life through his father's merit and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 尋轉沛郡。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為南主客郎中、太尉屬，襲爵雲陽伯。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director in the Southern Reception Bureau and Clerk to the Grand Commandant, and inherited the title Earl of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director in the Southern Reception Bureau and Clerk to the Grand Commandant, and inherited the title of Earl of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，既克宛城，拜長猷南陽太守。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign and Wan City had been taken, Changyou was appointed Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign and Wan City had been taken, Changyou was appointed Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 及鑾輿將反，詔長猷曰：「昔曹公克荊州，留滿寵於後。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to return, an edict told Changyou: "In former times, when Duke Cao conquered Jing Province, he left Man Chong behind.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to turn back, an edict addressed Changyou: "When Duke Cao of Wei conquered Jing Province, he left Man Chong behind to hold it.

sentences.zh: 朕今委卿此郡，兼統戎馬，非直綏初附，以扞城相託。」

translations.literal: I now entrust this commandery to you and also give you command of the troops; this is not merely to soothe those newly attached, but to leave the defense of the city in your hands."
translations.idiomatic: I now entrust this commandery to you together with command of the troops—not merely to pacify those newly attached, but to leave the city's defense in your hands."

sentences.zh: 特賜縑二百匹。

translations.literal: He was specially granted two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩於南陽，斂於其郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xiaowen died at Nanyang and was encoffined in that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen died at Nanyang and was laid in state in that commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋徵護軍長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to serve as chief clerk to the Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to serve as chief clerk to the Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，壽春歸欵，兼給事黃門侍郎，持節宣慰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, when Shouchun submitted, he was additionally made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent with imperial credentials to announce and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, when Shouchun submitted, he was additionally made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent with imperial credentials to announce the court's favor and offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 及任城王為揚州刺史，詔長猷為諮議參軍，帶安豐太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Rencheng became Prefect of Yang Province, an edict made Changyou a Consulting Advisor and acting Administrator of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Rencheng became Prefect of Yang Province, an edict appointed Changyou Consulting Advisor and acting Administrator of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 轉徐州武昌王府長史，帶彭城內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk in the household of the Prince of Wuchang in Xuzhou, with the additional post of Interior Minister of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk in the household of the Prince of Wuchang in Xuzhou, while also serving as Interior Minister of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 徵拜諫議大夫，轉司徒諮議，遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Remonstrating Grand Master, transferred to Consulting Advisor to the Minister of Education, and promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Remonstrating Grand Master, transferred to Consulting Advisor to the Minister of Education, and promoted to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 永平五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 諡曰貞侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 子廓，襲。

translations.literal: His son Kuo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuo inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子元休，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yuanxiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanxiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 興和中，睢州刺史。

translations.literal: During Xinghe, Prefect of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he served as Prefect of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 元休弟憑，字元祐。

translations.literal: Yuanxiu's younger brother Ping, styled Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxiu's younger brother Ping, courtesy name Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 武定中，司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: During Wuding, Attendant Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as Attendant Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：游明根雅道儒風，終受非常之遇，以太和之盛，當乞言之重，抑亦曠世一時。

translations.literal: The historian writes: You Minggen embodied the refined way of the Confucian tradition and in the end received extraordinary favor; in the glory of the Taihe era, to bear the weight of remonstrance—this was indeed a pairing rare across ages.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: You Minggen embodied the refined way of the Confucian tradition and ultimately received extraordinary favor; in the glory of the Taihe era, to bear the weight of remonstrance was a pairing rare across the ages.

sentences.zh: 肇既聿修，克隆堂構，正情梗氣，顛沛不渝，辭爵主幼之年，亢節臣權之日，顧視羣公，其風固以遠矣。

translations.literal: Zhao carried forward what had been begun and enlarged the family estate; upright in sentiment and unyielding in spirit, he did not waver through hardship; he declined enfeoffment in the years when the sovereign was young and held to lofty integrity when ministers held power—looking back at the other lords, his conduct was indeed far above them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao carried forward what had been begun and enlarged the family estate; upright in sentiment and unyielding in spirit, he did not waver through hardship. He declined enfeoffment while the sovereign was still young and held to lofty integrity when powerful ministers ruled the court—compared with the other lords, his conduct stood far above them.

sentences.zh: 劉芳矯然特立，沉深好古，博通洽識，為世儒宗，亦當年之師表也。

translations.literal: Liu Fang stood apart with striking distinction, deep and devoted to antiquity, broadly learned and thoroughly knowledgeable—a patriarch among scholars of the age and a model teacher for his generation as well.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang stood apart with striking distinction, deep and devoted to antiquity, broadly learned and thoroughly knowledgeable—the patriarch of scholars in his age and a model teacher for his generation.

sentences.zh: 懋才流識學，有名士之風。

translations.literal: Mao possessed talent, discernment, and learning, with the bearing of a distinguished scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Mao possessed talent, discernment, and learning, with the bearing of a distinguished scholar.

sentences.zh: 見重於世，不虛然矣。

translations.literal: That he was held in esteem by the world was no empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: That the age held him in high esteem was no empty reputation.

translations.literal: Regarding the edict dispatching the three armies of the southern campaign at the west of the Mian, Qiucheng, and Liankou — note: the so-called "three armies of the southern campaign" refers to the campaigns of the eighth month of the fourth year of Taihe, which concerned the contest for Jiaocheng and had nothing to do with the west of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: On the edict dispatching the three armies of the southern campaign at the west of the Mian, Qiucheng, and Liankou: the so-called "three armies of the southern campaign" refers to the fighting of the eighth month in the fourth year of Taihe, which concerned the contest for Jiaocheng and had nothing to do with the west of the Mian.

translations.literal: According to juan 7, Part 1, Annals of the Emperor Xiaowen, Part 1, at that time the Wei forces had routes "out from Qucheng," "out from Haixi," "out from Liankou," "out from Jiaocheng," and "out from Xia'cai."
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 7, Part 1, Annals of the Emperor Xiaowen, Part 1, the Wei forces at that time had routes "out from Qucheng," "out from Haixi," "out from Liankou," "out from Jiaocheng," and "out from Xia'cai."

sentences.zh: 海西、朐城、連口都在今江蘇海州東南。

translations.literal: Haixi, Qucheng, and Liankou were all southeast of present-day Haizhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi, Qucheng, and Liankou all lay southeast of present-day Haizhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 這裏「沔西」當是「海西」之訛，「仇城」是「朐城」之訛。

translations.idiomatic: Here "west of the Mian" is likely a corruption of "Haixi," and "Qiucheng" (the cited text) is likely a corruption of "Qucheng" (the cited text).

translations.idiomatic: On "had already granted his petition for redress": Cefu, juan 899

translations.idiomatic: Note: the present transmitted Rites of Zhou, Grand Minister of Education, has the character "the cited text."

translations.idiomatic: On "the Yuxiang stands in the four outskirts of the realm": various editions write "the cited text" for "the cited text"; the Northern History, juan 42, writes "the cited text."

sentences.zh: 按今傳本禮記王制、內則都作「西郊」。

translations.literal: Note: present transmitted texts of the Record of Rites, "Royal Regulations" and "Inner Canon," both read "western outskirts."
translations.idiomatic: Note: present transmitted texts of the Record of Rites, "Royal Regulations" and "Inner Canon," both read "western outskirts."

sentences.zh: 孫志祖讀書脞錄續錄引北史此傳，以為傳本禮記作「西郊」誤。

translations.literal: Sun Zhizu, in the Xulu and Xulu sequels to his Dushu Suolu, cites this biography from the Northern History and holds that the transmitted Record of Rites reading "western outskirts" is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhizu, in the Xulu and Xulu sequels to his Dushu Suolu, cites this biography from the Northern History and holds that the transmitted Record of Rites reading "western outskirts" is erroneous.

sentences.zh: 孫說是非，今可不論，但據劉芳疏此段本說四門置學事，上文明言「四小在郊」，下文引鄭注，又言「四學，周四郊之虞庠也」。

translations.literal: Whether Sun's view is right or wrong need not be discussed here; but according to Liu Fang's exposition, this passage originally concerns establishing schools at the four gates; the text above clearly states "the four xiao are in the outskirts," and the commentarial passage below again reads "the four schools are the Yuxiang of the four weekly outskirts."
translations.idiomatic: Whether Sun's view is right or wrong need not be discussed here; but according to Liu Fang's exposition, this passage originally concerns establishing schools at the four gates—the text above clearly states "the four xiao are in the outskirts," and the commentarial passage below again reads "the four schools are the Yuxiang of the four weekly outskirts."

sentences.zh: 則劉芳所據禮記本作「四郊」，這裏「西」字當是後人所改，今據北史回改。

translations.literal: Liu Fang's Record of Rites text therefore read "four outskirts"; the character "the cited text" here was likely altered by a later hand, and is now restored according to the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang's Record of Rites text therefore read "four outskirts"; the character "the cited text" here was likely altered by a later hand and is now restored according to the Northern History.

translations.idiomatic: On "the fifth year of Emperor Gaozu": Hanshu, juan 25, Part 1, Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices, Part 1

sentences.zh: 大將軍攻討 按卷八０樊子鵠傳，當時領兵攻子鵠、劉粹者是婁昭，他不是「大將軍」，且下無人名，「將」字當衍。

translations.literal: "The Grand General attacked and punished" - note: according to juan 80, biography of Fan Zihu, the one then leading troops against Zihu and Liu Cui was Lou Zhao; he was not "Grand General," and with no personal name following below, the character "the cited text" is likely superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: On "the Grand General attacked and punished": according to juan 80, biography of Fan Zihu, the commander then leading troops against Zihu and Liu Cui was Lou Zhao; he was not "Grand General," and with no personal name following below, the character "the cited text" is likely superfluous.
